# Purpose

This notebook builds the Study 1 supplementary material. It writes each
supplementary table as a LaTeX fragment, a small `.tex` file that the
supplement section of the manuscript pulls in with `\input{}`, and it copies
the supplementary figures beside them.

It runs no analysis of its own. It reads the files below. A table marked
"registered completion set" is one the preregistration commits to reporting.

  - `study1_long_with_text.csv`                     (long-format ratings)
  - `models/study1_lmm_creativity.rds`              (creativity linear mixed model, LMM)
  - `models/study1_lmm_effort.rds`                  (effort LMM)
  - `tables/study1_specification_curve.csv`         (multiverse: the attribution estimate under many alternative specifications)
  - `tables/study1_brms_primary_fixed.csv`          (Bayesian replication)
  - `tables/study1_brms_cumulative_fixed.csv`       (Bayesian ordinal version)
  - `tables/study1_lmm_fixed_effects.csv`           (lmerTest coefficients, for the brms-vs-lmer tolerance)
  - `tables/study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv`     (equivalence at the wider bounds; Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 3)
  - `tables/study1_text_effort_prevalence.csv`      (effort-talk rates; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_creativity_prevalence.csv`  (creativity-talk rates; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_prompt_by_arm.csv`          (prompting-and-generating talk by arm; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_demo_*.csv`                      (demographics)
  - `tables/study1_exclusion_flow.csv`              (exclusion flow, incl. step-0 preview row)
  - `tables/study1_joint_model_anova.csv`           (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_lmm_fully_maximal.csv`           (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_balance.csv`                     (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_attrition_by_condition.csv`      (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_bootstrap_d.csv`                 (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_influence_lopo.csv`, `_loso.csv` (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_h4_variance_partition.csv`       (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_confirmatory_family.csv`         (registered completion set; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_h2_ordinal.csv`                  (H2 in the cumulative-link model beside the raw-scale contrast; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_h4_resolution.csv`               (sampling spread of the H4 ratio estimate at this design's arm sizes, by simulation; Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_denotation_tests.csv`       (the five registered tests on the written explanations; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_denotation_slope_sensitivity.csv` (the same five tests refitted with a participant random slope, the sensitivity check the preregistration lists beside them; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd section 7.2)
  - `tables/study1_h3_equivalence.csv`             (the registered H3 equivalence test under both random-effects structures; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10)
  - `tables/study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv`        (the power of the H3 equivalence test by simulation, at the registered and the descriptive bounds; Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 4)
  - `tables/study1_text_recoverability.csv`         (how far the rating and the arm can be recovered from the words, and what the words add to the rating in recovering the arm; one of the two checks run in every study; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv`  (within-person word overlap by arm with its Holm-corrected reading, the text version of H4; the other check run in every study; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_item_sensitivity.csv`            (the registered contrasts with the effort item whose scale wording differs set aside; Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_novelty_within_between.csv` (familiarity talk and the creativity rating, split into a within-person and a between-person part; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_affect_by_arm.csv`          (valence, arousal, dominance and concreteness of the explanations, by arm; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_topics_by_arm.csv`          (topic weights of the explanations, by arm; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_prediction_weights.csv`     (the words the recoverability models weight most heavily; Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/text_topics_top_words.csv`, `tables/text_topics_stability.csv`, `tables/text_topics_embedding_agreement.csv` (each topic's top words, the stability rule that set the number of topics, and the embedding check on the topics; Study1_02_Text.ipynb)
  - `tables/study1_quant_run_manifest.csv`, `tables/study1_text_run_manifest.csv`, `tables/study1_integration_run_manifest.csv`, `tables/study1_text_manifest.csv`, `tables/study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv` (each upstream stage's record of what its last run wrote; read when present)

Some inputs are required: the demographics, the exclusion flow, the two model
fits, and the tables behind the multiverse and Bayesian rows of
Supplementary Table 1. The notebook stops if one of them is missing. Every
other table is guarded. Each chunk deletes its own `.tex` fragment before it
reads anything, so any fragment on disk was written by the latest knit (the
latest rendering of this file). A guarded table can be pending for two
reasons. It may not have been produced yet. Or the run manifest of the stage
that produces it, which is that stage's record of what its last run wrote,
may not record it as written by that run. Either way its
subsection prints a `pending:` line naming the notebook that writes it, and
the rest of the supplement still builds.

The notebook writes:

  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_1_robustness.tex`     (Supp Table 1)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_2_text_rates.tex`     (Supp Table 2)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_3_prompt_talk.tex`    (Supp Table 3)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_demographics.tex`     (extra: demographics)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_exclusions.tex`       (extra: exclusion flow)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_full_lmm.tex`         (extra: full LMM coefs)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_joint_model.tex`      (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_fully_maximal.tex`    (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_balance.tex`          (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_attrition.tex`        (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_bootstrap_d.tex`      (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_influence.tex`        (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_h4_variance.tex`     (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_holm_family.tex`     (registered completion set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_h2_ordinal.tex`       (H2, raw-scale and ordinal versions)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_h4_resolution.tex`    (H4, sampling spread of the ratio estimate by simulation)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_denotation_tests.tex` (five registered text tests, Benjamini-Hochberg corrected)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_denotation_slope_sensitivity.tex` (the five text tests refitted with a participant random slope)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_h3_equivalence.tex`  (H3, the registered equivalence test under both random-effects structures)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_h3_equivalence_power.tex` (H3, the power of the equivalence test by simulation)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_recoverability.tex` (the two checks run in every study: rating and arm recovered from the words)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.tex` (the two checks run in every study: within-person word overlap by arm)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_item_sensitivity.tex` (the effort item whose scale wording differs)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_novelty_within_between.tex` (familiarity talk, within and between participants)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_affect_by_arm.tex` (word-norm scores of the explanations by arm)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_topics_stability.tex` (how the number of topics was set)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_topics_by_arm.tex` (topic weights by arm, labelled by top words)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_topics_embedding_agreement.tex` (the embedding check on the topics)
  - `supplement/tables/sup_table_text_prediction_weights.tex` (the most heavily weighted words)
  - `supplement/figures/sup_fig_1a_specification_creativity.pdf`, `sup_fig_1b_specification_effort.pdf` (Supp Fig 1)
  - `supplement/figures/sup_fig_2_brms_ppc.pdf`       (Supp Fig 2)
  - `tables/study1_supplements_run_manifest.csv`      (this knit's run record: every file read and written, with its fingerprint and status)

The figure PDFs are copied unchanged from the analysis outputs in
`Analysis/.../Study 1/figures/`.

# 1. Setup

```{r paths}
# PROJECT_ROOT is the first folder at or above this file's own folder, the
# working directory when the file is knitted, that holds both Data and
# Analysis; the environment variable STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT, when set, names it
# instead.
PROJECT_ROOT <- local({
  is_root <- function(p) dir.exists(file.path(p, "Data")) &&
                         dir.exists(file.path(p, "Analysis"))
  root <- Sys.getenv("STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT")
  if (nzchar(root)) {
    root <- normalizePath(root, mustWork = FALSE)
    if (!is_root(root)) {
      stop("The folder STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT names has no Data and Analysis ",
           "folders.")
    }
  } else {
    root <- normalizePath(getwd(), mustWork = TRUE)
    while (!is_root(root)) {
      if (identical(dirname(root), root)) {
        stop("No folder at or above the working directory holds both Data ",
             "and Analysis. Knit this file from its own folder, or set ",
             "STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT to the project root.")
      }
      root <- dirname(root)
    }
  }
  root
})

STUDY_NUM    <- 1
STUDY_FOLDER <- paste("Study", STUDY_NUM)

PATH_ANALYSIS    <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "Analysis",
                              "R Analysis Pipeline", STUDY_FOLDER)
PATH_OUT         <- PATH_ANALYSIS
PATH_OUT_FIG     <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "figures")
PATH_OUT_TAB     <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "tables")
PATH_OUT_MODELS  <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "models")
PATH_OUT_NLP     <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "nlp")

# Paper-side outputs. The supplement has its own subfolder, apart from the
# main-text figures and tables.
PATH_PAPER       <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "Docs", "Writing", "Final Paper")
PATH_SUP         <- file.path(PATH_PAPER, "supplement")
PATH_SUP_TAB     <- file.path(PATH_SUP, "tables")
PATH_SUP_FIG     <- file.path(PATH_SUP, "figures")

# The run record of this knit sits beside the analysis tables, under the name
# every stage of the pipeline uses: tables/study1_<stage>_run_manifest.csv.
PATH_RUN_MANIFEST <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_supplements_run_manifest.csv")

if (!dir.exists(PROJECT_ROOT)) {
  stop("PROJECT_ROOT does not exist:\n  ", PROJECT_ROOT,
       "\nIs Google Drive mounted? Edit PROJECT_ROOT to point to your copy.")
}

for (p in c(PATH_SUP, PATH_SUP_TAB, PATH_SUP_FIG)) {
  dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

cat("Supplement outputs will be written to:\n  ", PATH_SUP, "\n")
```

```{r theme-and-helpers}
PAL_TYPE <- c("Human" = "#A1A1A1", "AI" = "#3E3E3E")

theme_paper <- function(base_size = 11) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "none",
      strip.background   = element_blank(),
      strip.text         = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      axis.line          = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks         = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.text          = element_text(color = "black"),
      panel.grid         = element_blank()
    )
}

# fmt_p() and fmt_n() are vectorised: each formats every element of its
# input. A length mismatch between two extracted values therefore shows up in
# the output, where R would otherwise recycle the shorter one without a
# warning. The scalar() guard below turns such a mismatch into an error
# wherever a single value is required.

# Format p-values: three decimals, or "< 0.001" below that (vectorised).
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  vapply(p, function(pi) {
    if (is.na(pi))       "NA"
    else if (pi < 0.001) "< 0.001"
    else                 sprintf("%.3f", pi)
  }, character(1))
}

# Format numbers with a set number of decimal places (vectorised).
fmt_n <- function(x, d = 2) {
  vapply(x, function(xi) {
    if (is.na(xi)) "NA"
    else           sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), xi)
  }, character(1))
}

# Guard: check that an extracted value is exactly one value and is not NA.
# Every `pull()` or `[` extraction that feeds sprintf() goes through it, so a
# filter that matches 0 or 2 rows stops the knit with an error.
scalar <- function(x, what = "value") {
  if (length(x) != 1L) {
    stop(sprintf("Expected exactly one %s but got length %d. ",
                 what, length(x)),
         "Check the filter/key that produced it.")
  }
  if (is.na(x)) stop(sprintf("Extracted %s is NA.", what))
  x
}

# A p-value with its relation sign, for sentences: "< 0.001" or "= 0.012".
# fmt_p() alone returns "< 0.001" for a small p, which would read as
# "p = < 0.001" if the sign were typed into the sentence.
p_rel <- function(p) {
  ifelse(is.na(p), "= NA", ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", fmt_p(p))))
}
```

```{r run-record}
# Every knit gets a run identifier and keeps a ledger of the files it read
# and wrote. The last chunk writes the ledger to
# tables/study1_supplements_run_manifest.csv, one row per file. A row holds
# the run identifier, the stage, and the role of the file: this source file,
# an input table, an upstream run manifest, or an output fragment or figure.
# It also holds the file's path within the project, its size, and its
# SHA-256 fingerprint, a 64-character code computed from the file's bytes
# that changes if a single byte changes. Last come a status (read, absent,
# not current, written or pending) and a note. The manifest of an earlier
# knit is deleted here, before anything else is written. A knit that stops
# partway therefore leaves no manifest saying that it finished.
RUN_STAGE   <- "supplements"
RUN_STARTED <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z")
RUN_ID      <- paste0(RUN_STAGE, "-", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%dT%H%M%S"), "-",
                      substr(digest::digest(c(RUN_STARTED, Sys.getpid())), 1, 8))
unlink(PATH_RUN_MANIFEST)

# The file being knitted; when the code is run outside a knit, the copy in
# the analysis folder is fingerprinted in its place.
SOURCE_FILE <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
if (is.null(SOURCE_FILE)) {
  SOURCE_FILE <- file.path(PATH_ANALYSIS, "Study1_Supplements.Rmd")
}

file_sha256 <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NA_character_)
  digest::digest(file = path, algo = "sha256")
}

# Paths are stored relative to PROJECT_ROOT so the manifest reads the same on
# any machine.
path_in_project <- function(path) {
  root <- paste0(PROJECT_ROOT, "/")
  ifelse(startsWith(path, root), substring(path, nchar(root) + 1L), path)
}

# The fingerprint and size are taken from the full path before the row is
# built, because tibble() lets a later argument see an earlier column, and
# the path column holds the project-relative form.
run_ledger <- list()
record_file <- function(role, path, status, note = "") {
  sha   <- file_sha256(path)
  bytes <- if (file.exists(path)) file.size(path) else NA_real_
  run_ledger[[length(run_ledger) + 1L]] <<- tibble(
    run_id = RUN_ID, stage = RUN_STAGE, role = role,
    path   = path_in_project(path), status = status,
    sha256 = sha, bytes = bytes, note = note
  )
  invisible(NULL)
}
record_file("source", SOURCE_FILE, "knitted")

# Each output is deleted before its chunk reads anything, so a chunk that
# ends pending, or stops on a failed check, leaves no fragment from an
# earlier knit for the manuscript to pick up.
remove_fragment <- function(tex_name) {
  unlink(file.path(PATH_SUP_TAB, tex_name))
}
write_fragment <- function(tex, tex_name) {
  path <- file.path(PATH_SUP_TAB, tex_name)
  cat(tex, file = path)
  record_file("output", path, "written")
  cat("Wrote ", tex_name, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r upstream-manifests}
# Each upstream stage writes a run manifest, its record of the files its last
# run wrote. Suppose the manifest of the stage that writes a table is on disk
# and does not record that table as written by its run. The table is then
# treated as pending here, even if a file of that name is present, since the
# file may be left over from an earlier run.
#
# UPSTREAM_MANIFESTS lists the manifests read, by stage. The integration stage
# has two: its run manifest, and tables/study1_text_manifest.csv, the list of
# text-program outputs that Study1_03_Integration.Rmd writes beside it. The
# text stage is Study1_02_Text.ipynb, whose manifest covers the files it
# writes under nlp/ and tables/.
#
# The manifests come in three layouts, and each is read in its own way.
#   (a) A path (or file) column and a status column, as in the integration
#       and robustness run manifests. The status is read as written.
#       UPSTREAM_OK_STATUS holds the status words read as a successful write.
#       Any other status makes the table pending, and the console prints it,
#       so a difference in wording between stages shows on screen.
#   (b) A file column and a written_this_run column with no status column, as
#       in the quant run manifest and the text manifest. TRUE is read as
#       "written" and FALSE as "not written this run"; a blank is read as
#       "not recorded" and makes the table pending. When the manifest also
#       has an exists column, FALSE there is read as "absent".
#   (c) A file column and a sha256 column with neither a status nor a
#       written_this_run column, as in the text notebook's run manifest.
#       Every row is a file that run wrote, beside the SHA-256 checksum the
#       file had when the run wrote it. The file on disk is read as written
#       when its checksum matches the row, and as "changed since the run"
#       when it does not, since a file whose checksum differs was not written
#       by the run the manifest records.
# When a manifest has a role column, only its output rows are read, so a
# table a stage only read is not taken for one it wrote. A manifest in none
# of these layouts is recorded with the columns it has, and the tables it
# lists are read without a run check. So is a table that no manifest of its
# stage lists, and this knit's manifest notes it. The last chunk names every
# input read without a run check.
UPSTREAM_MANIFESTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~stage,        ~manifest,
  "quant",       "study1_quant_run_manifest.csv",
  "text",        "study1_text_run_manifest.csv",
  "integration", "study1_integration_run_manifest.csv",
  "integration", "study1_text_manifest.csv",
  "robustness",  "study1_robustness_run_manifest.csv"
)
UPSTREAM_OK_STATUS <- c("ok", "written", "success", "succeeded", "complete",
                        "completed", "current", "pass", "passed", "done")

read_upstream_manifest <- function(st, manifest) {
  mp <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, manifest)
  if (!file.exists(mp)) {
    cat("No run manifest on disk for the ", st, " stage (", manifest,
        "); the tables it would list are read without a run check.\n", sep = "")
    record_file("upstream manifest", mp, "absent")
    return(NULL)
  }
  m <- read_csv(mp, show_col_types = FALSE,
                col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
  path_col <- intersect(c("path", "file", "output", "output_path", "filename"),
                        names(m))[1]
  role_col <- intersect(c("role", "kind", "type"), names(m))[1]
  if (!is.na(role_col)) {
    m <- m[grepl("output", m[[role_col]], ignore.case = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  }
  layout <- if (is.na(path_col))                   NA_character_
            else if ("status" %in% names(m))           "status"
            else if ("written_this_run" %in% names(m)) "written_this_run"
            else if ("sha256" %in% names(m))           "checksum"
            else                                       NA_character_
  if (is.na(layout)) {
    cat(manifest, " has no layout this check can read (found: ",
        paste(names(m), collapse = ", "),
        "); the tables it lists are read without a run check.\n", sep = "")
    record_file("upstream manifest", mp, "read", "no layout this check can read")
    return(NULL)
  }
  status <- switch(layout,
    status = tolower(trimws(m$status)),
    written_this_run = {
      w <- toupper(trimws(m$written_this_run))
      s <- ifelse(w %in% "TRUE", "written",
                  ifelse(w %in% "FALSE", "not written this run", "not recorded"))
      if ("exists" %in% names(m)) {
        s[toupper(trimws(m$exists)) %in% "FALSE"] <- "absent"
      }
      s
    },
    checksum = {
      # The manifest's paths are relative to the Study 1 analysis folder.
      on_disk <- vapply(file.path(PATH_ANALYSIS, m[[path_col]]), file_sha256,
                        character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
      ifelse(is.na(on_disk), "absent",
             ifelse(on_disk == tolower(trimws(m$sha256)), "written",
                    "changed since the run"))
    })
  run_note <- if ("run_id" %in% names(m) && nrow(m) > 0L)
    paste0("run ", paste(unique(m$run_id), collapse = "; "), "; ") else ""
  record_file("upstream manifest", mp, "read",
              paste0(run_note, "read through its ",
                     switch(layout,
                            status           = "status column",
                            written_this_run = "written_this_run column",
                            checksum         = "checksums")))
  tibble(stage    = st,
         manifest = manifest,
         basis    = layout,
         file     = basename(m[[path_col]]),
         status   = status)
}

upstream_index <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(UPSTREAM_MANIFESTS)), function(i) {
  read_upstream_manifest(UPSTREAM_MANIFESTS$stage[i],
                         UPSTREAM_MANIFESTS$manifest[i])
}))

# A table listed in two manifests of its stage must be recorded as written in
# both. A manifest that lists a file twice is read by its last row. The note
# names each manifest and what it records, and goes into this knit's manifest.
upstream_check <- function(csv_name, stage) {
  if (is.na(stage) || nrow(upstream_index) == 0L) {
    return(list(ok = TRUE, note = "read without a run check"))
  }
  hit <- upstream_index %>%
    filter(stage == !!stage, file == csv_name) %>%
    group_by(manifest) %>%
    slice_tail(n = 1) %>%
    ungroup()
  if (nrow(hit) == 0L) {
    return(list(ok = TRUE, note = "read without a run check"))
  }
  ok <- hit$status %in% UPSTREAM_OK_STATUS
  notes <- ifelse(
    hit$basis == "checksum",
    ifelse(ok,
           paste0(hit$manifest, " lists it and its checksum matches"),
           paste0(hit$manifest, " lists it, and the file on disk is '",
                  hit$status, "'")),
    ifelse(ok,
           paste0(hit$manifest, " records it as ", hit$status),
           paste0(hit$manifest, " records it as '", hit$status, "'")))
  list(ok = all(ok), note = paste(notes, collapse = "; "))
}
```

```{r table-helpers}
# Throughout this file, "the writer" of a table is the notebook that writes
# it, and a "column contract" is the list of columns that notebook is
# expected to deposit.
#
# render_prereg_table(), below, turns a guarded CSV into a .tex table. It
#   (a) deletes the table's .tex fragment, so nothing from an earlier knit
#       survives a pending or failed chunk,
#   (b) prints a "pending:" line and goes no further if the source CSV is not
#       on disk, or if the producing stage's run manifest does not record it
#       as written, so a half-built pipeline gives a shorter supplement and
#       not a broken one,
#   (c) formats p-value columns with fmt_p() and rounds the rest,
#   (d) writes the .tex and records it in the run ledger, and
#   (e) returns the formatted tibble for display.
# `transform` lets a caller reshape or summarise the table before formatting.
# `caption` is a string, or a function of the table as read, for a caption
# that quotes the writer's own description columns. `stage` names the stage
# whose run manifests are checked: "quant", "text", "integration",
# "robustness", or NA for a table with no stage manifest. `col_widths` names
# text columns to set at a fixed width, for example c(test = "5cm"), so that
# their cells wrap onto several lines and do not push the table past the
# page.
#
# The pattern below lists the p-value column names the writers in this
# pipeline use. Without it a p of 1e-4 would be rounded to three decimals and
# print as 0, not as "< 0.001". The final alternative, a name ending in "_p",
# covers the likelihood ratio p-values of the H4 variance test
# (lrt_between_p, lrt_residual_p). It also covers the two H4 columns the
# confirmatory family carries beside its own (h4_creativity_lrt_p,
# h4_effort_lrt_p). Every column ending in "_p" in the tables rendered here is
# a p-value.
P_COL_PATTERN <- paste0(
  "^(p|p\\.value|p_value|pval|Pr\\(>F\\)|p_fisher|p_chisq|p_adj|p_perm|",
  "p_maximal|p_holm|nhst_p|tost_p)$|^fisher_p_|^p_|_p$"
)

# The guarded read. Every table below goes through it, including the tables
# a chunk builds itself instead of rendering a CSV as deposited. It returns
# NULL, and says why, when the file is absent or its stage's run manifest
# does not record it as written. Otherwise it records the file in the run
# ledger, with the note of the run check, and returns it.
read_table_or_null <- function(csv_name, pending_msg, stage = NA_character_) {
  path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, csv_name)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    cat("pending: ", pending_msg, " (missing ", csv_name, ")\n", sep = "")
    record_file("input", path, "absent")
    return(NULL)
  }
  chk <- upstream_check(csv_name, stage)
  if (!chk$ok) {
    cat("pending: ", pending_msg, " (", csv_name, " is on disk, but ",
        chk$note, ")\n", sep = "")
    record_file("input", path, "not current", chk$note)
    return(NULL)
  }
  record_file("input", path, "read", chk$note)
  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

render_prereg_table <- function(csv_name, tex_name, caption, label,
                                pending_msg, digits = 3,
                                transform = identity, stage = NA_character_,
                                col_widths = NULL) {
  remove_fragment(tex_name)
  df <- read_table_or_null(csv_name, pending_msg, stage)
  if (is.null(df)) {
    record_file("output", file.path(PATH_SUP_TAB, tex_name), "pending",
                pending_msg)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if (is.function(caption)) caption <- caption(df)
  df <- transform(df)
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) {
    stop(csv_name, " exists but has zero rows after transform; ",
         "re-run the producing notebook (", pending_msg, ").")
  }
  df_fmt <- df %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & matches(P_COL_PATTERN), fmt_p),
           across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits)))
  tex <- df_fmt %>%
    knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
                 caption = caption, label = label) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position",
                                                "scale_down"),
                              font_size = 9)
  # Each column named in col_widths, and present in the table, is set at
  # its fixed width. A name the table lacks is skipped.
  for (nm in intersect(names(col_widths), names(df_fmt))) {
    tex <- kableExtra::column_spec(tex, which(names(df_fmt) == nm),
                                   width = col_widths[[nm]])
  }
  write_fragment(tex, tex_name)
  df_fmt
}

# Several writers put one sentence in a column and repeat it on every row,
# for example the reference distribution of a test or the definition of a
# contrast. Typeset in every cell, such a column makes the table wide and
# adds nothing the caption does not say. This helper takes those columns out
# of the typeset table and prints each one once on the console. The deposited
# CSV is not changed. A column counts as a long constant when it is text, has
# no NA, takes one value on every row, and that value is at least `min_chars`
# characters long. Columns named in `keep` stay in place whatever their
# content, for a column that a caption names or that later code reads. The
# helper is used through `transform` in the H4 variance, H2 ordinal, H3,
# resolution and power tables below, and in sections 11.2 to 11.5.
drop_long_constant_columns <- function(df, min_chars = 40L,
                                       keep = character(0)) {
  is_long_constant <- vapply(df, function(col) {
    is.character(col) && !anyNA(col) && dplyr::n_distinct(col) == 1L &&
      nchar(col[1]) >= min_chars
  }, logical(1))
  is_long_constant[names(df) %in% keep] <- FALSE
  if (any(is_long_constant)) {
    cat("Constant text columns kept out of the typeset table:\n")
    for (nm in names(df)[is_long_constant]) {
      cat("  ", nm, ": ", df[[nm]][1], "\n", sep = "")
    }
  }
  df[, !is_long_constant, drop = FALSE]
}

# Some tables need a different helper. The two tables of section 10.13 carry
# several text columns that differ between rows, such as the name of the
# statistic, the model and the shuffle behind the null. No column is
# constant, so the helper above removes nothing. The Holm table of section
# 10.8, the random-slope table of section 10.11 and the item sensitivity
# table of section 11.1 carry per-row notes and fit records beside the
# numbers a reader checks. Typeset as deposited, each of these tables runs to
# eleven columns or more, too many for scale_down to fit on a page at a
# readable size. This helper keeps the columns named in `keep`, in that
# order. It prints every other column once on the console, beside the
# row-identifying columns in `key`, so each deposited value still appears in
# the knitted output. The deposited CSV is not changed. A name in `keep` that
# the writer did not deposit is reported and skipped, and the render goes on.
keep_columns_report <- function(df, keep, key = keep[1]) {
  absent <- setdiff(keep, names(df))
  if (length(absent) > 0L) {
    cat("Columns named for the typeset table but not deposited: ",
        paste(absent, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  }
  keep    <- intersect(keep, names(df))
  dropped <- setdiff(names(df), keep)
  if (length(dropped) > 0L) {
    cat("Columns kept out of the typeset table, printed here once:\n")
    df %>%
      select(all_of(c(intersect(key, names(df)), dropped))) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
  }
  df[, keep, drop = FALSE]
}

# Captions go to LaTeX as written. Text quoted into a caption from a
# writer's own columns therefore has LaTeX's special characters escaped
# first. kable escapes the typeset cells itself.
latex_escape <- function(x) {
  # Backslashes are set aside first, so the braces of the commands that
  # replace them are not escaped in turn.
  x <- gsub("\\", "\001", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("([&%$#_{}])", "\\\\\\1", x)
  x <- gsub("~", "\002", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("^", "\003", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\001", "\\textbackslash{}", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\002", "\\textasciitilde{}", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("\003", "\\textasciicircum{}", x, fixed = TRUE)
}

# For the tables of section 11, whose writers describe their own model in a
# text column. The helper returns one sentence quoting the distinct values of
# that column, so the caption states the model in the writer's terms. It
# returns an empty string when the column is absent or empty.
writer_quote <- function(df, col, lead) {
  if (!col %in% names(df)) return("")
  v <- unique(stats::na.omit(as.character(df[[col]])))
  if (length(v) == 0L) return("")
  paste0(" ", lead, ": ", paste(latex_escape(v), collapse = "; "), ".")
}
```

# 2. Demographics table

```{r demographics-table}
remove_fragment("sup_table_demographics.tex")

# Read the per-attribute demographic CSVs. These are required: read_csv()
# stops on a missing file.
read_demo <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, paste0("study1_demo_", name, ".csv"))
  d <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  record_file("input", path, "read", upstream_check(basename(path), "quant")$note)
  d
}

age   <- read_demo("age")
gen   <- read_demo("gender")
race  <- read_demo("race")
exper <- read_demo("experience")
bal   <- read_demo("balance")

# The analytic N is the sum of the counts in the condition-balance CSV. The
# check fixes it at the project N, so a change in the upstream exclusion flow
# stops the knit here and never reaches a caption.
stopifnot(all(c("Type", "n") %in% names(bal)))
n_analytic <- sum(as.integer(bal$n))
stopifnot(n_analytic == 111L)   # analytic N (56 Human / 55 AI)

# Age summary, read by name. The CSV header starts with `n` (n, mean_age,
# sd_age, min_age, max_age), so a read by position would take the participant
# count for the mean. The required columns are checked before anything is
# extracted.
age_req <- c("n", "mean_age", "sd_age", "min_age", "max_age")
if (!all(age_req %in% names(age))) {
  stop("study1_demo_age.csv is missing expected columns. Expected: ",
       paste(age_req, collapse = ", "), "; found: ",
       paste(names(age), collapse = ", "),
       ". Re-run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 3.1 (demographics).")
}
stopifnot(nrow(age) == 1L)
n_age    <- as.integer(scalar(age$n,        "age n"))
age_M    <- as.numeric(scalar(age$mean_age, "mean_age"))
age_SD   <- as.numeric(scalar(age$sd_age,   "sd_age"))
age_Min  <- as.numeric(scalar(age$min_age,  "min_age"))
age_Max  <- as.numeric(scalar(age$max_age,  "max_age"))
stopifnot(age_Min <= age_M, age_M <= age_Max, age_SD >= 0, n_age <= n_analytic)

# The analytic N and the number reporting age differ (one participant did
# not report age). The table states both.
age_line <- sprintf("M = %.1f (SD = %.1f), range %g–%g; n = %d reporting",
                    age_M, age_SD, age_Min, age_Max, n_age)

# Attribute rows are built by name, from the `n` column. An attribute with
# fewer reporters than the analytic N states its own n, and the label suffix
# is chosen from the data. Percentages are of the analytic N, so the rows
# within an attribute sum to at most 100%.
demo_rows <- function(df, attribute) {
  stopifnot("n" %in% names(df), ncol(df) >= 2L)
  level_col <- setdiff(names(df), "n")[1]
  n_report  <- sum(as.integer(df$n))
  stopifnot(n_report <= n_analytic)
  attr_lab  <- if (n_report < n_analytic) {
    sprintf("%s (n = %d reporting)", attribute, n_report)
  } else attribute
  tibble(Attribute = attr_lab,
         Level     = as.character(df[[level_col]]),
         n         = as.integer(df$n),
         pct       = as.integer(df$n) / n_analytic * 100)
}

# Build a single combined table for the supplement.
demo_long <- bind_rows(
  tibble(Attribute = "Age",
         Level     = age_line,
         n         = NA_integer_,
         pct       = NA_real_),
  demo_rows(gen,   "Gender"),
  demo_rows(race,  "Race"),
  demo_rows(exper, "Art training"),
  demo_rows(bal,   "Condition")
)

# Format counts and percentages
demo_display <- demo_long %>%
  mutate(
    `n (%)` = ifelse(is.na(n), Level,
                     sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, pct)),
    Level   = ifelse(is.na(n), "", Level)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Attribute, Level, `n (%)`)

# Save as LaTeX
demo_display %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format    = "latex",
    booktabs  = TRUE,
    longtable = FALSE,
    caption   = sprintf(paste0(
      "Demographics of the Study 1 analytic sample (N = %d). ",
      "Percentages are of the analytic N; attributes with fewer reporters ",
      "state their own n."), n_analytic),
    label     = "supp_demographics"
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                            font_size = 9) %>%
  kableExtra::collapse_rows(columns = 1, latex_hline = "major") %>%
  write_fragment("sup_table_demographics.tex")

demo_display
```

# 3. Exclusion flow table

```{r exclusion-flow-table}
remove_fragment("sup_table_exclusions.tex")
excl_path  <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_exclusion_flow.csv")
exclusions <- read_csv(excl_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
record_file("input", excl_path, "read",
            upstream_check(basename(excl_path), "quant")$note)

# The exclusion CSV from Study1_01_Quant.Rmd opens with a step-0 row for the
# Qualtrics "Survey Preview" records, which have a blank participant id. One
# row per exclusion step follows: previews, unfinished, non-serious. The
# table is rendered from the CSV as it stands, with no rows added or
# dropped. Only its structure is checked here, including that the final n
# equals the analytic N.
excl_req <- c("step", "n")
if (!all(excl_req %in% names(exclusions))) {
  stop("study1_exclusion_flow.csv is missing expected columns (",
       paste(excl_req, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
       paste(names(exclusions), collapse = ", "),
       ". Re-run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 3.")
}
stopifnot(nrow(exclusions) >= 2L, !any(is.na(exclusions$n)))
n_final_flow <- as.integer(exclusions$n[nrow(exclusions)])
if (n_final_flow != n_analytic) {
  stop(sprintf(paste0("Final row of the exclusion flow (n = %d) does not ",
                      "equal the analytic N (%d). Re-run ",
                      "Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 3 so the flow and the ",
                      "demographics CSVs come from the same run."),
               n_final_flow, n_analytic))
}

# The caption is chosen from the data, so it never describes a row the table
# lacks. When the CSV has no step-0 row, the caption carries a PENDING note
# that shows in the typeset supplement, and it promises no step 0.
has_step0 <- any(grepl("\\(0\\)", exclusions$step))
if (!has_step0) {
  message("NOTE: study1_exclusion_flow.csv has no step-0 (Survey Preview) ",
          "row; re-run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 3.")
}
excl_caption <- if (has_step0) {
  "Study 1 exclusion flow. Step 0 removes Qualtrics survey-preview records (no participant id); subsequent steps are applied in order."
} else {
  "Study 1 exclusion flow (steps applied in order). PENDING: this table has no step-0 survey-preview row; re-run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 3 to add it (expected flow 119, 117, 114, 111)."
}

# Render
exclusions %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format    = "latex",
    booktabs  = TRUE,
    caption   = excl_caption,
    label     = "supp_exclusions"
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                            font_size = 9) %>%
  write_fragment("sup_table_exclusions.tex")

exclusions
```

# 4. Supplementary Table 1: Robustness summary

Supplementary Table 1 is the main robustness table for Study 1. Its first two
rows give the registered H1 quantity: the attribution contrast, averaged over
the two image kinds. The rows after them collect the multiverse checks, the
Bayesian refits, and the equivalence checks, which ask whether an estimate
lies inside a stated bound. Each of those rows reports a quantity related to
H1 but different from it, and its label names that quantity. None of them is
a second estimate of the H1 contrast. Every cell is computed from a pipeline
CSV, and no number in the table is typed by hand.

```{r supp-table-1}
remove_fragment("sup_table_1_robustness.tex")

# ---- The registered H1 contrast ---------------------------------------------
# H1 is the Human-minus-machine difference in mean rating, estimated from
# each dimension's primary mixed model and averaged with equal weight over
# the two image kinds. The confirmatory family (section 10.8) tests it. Its
# two rows open the table, so every row below can be read against the
# quantity the main text cites.
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.9):
# hypothesis, test, estimate, se, df, statistic, statistic_type, p_raw,
# p_holm, survives_holm_at_05, family_size, correction, h4_creativity_lrt_p,
# h4_effort_lrt_p. The dimension of each H1 row is read from its test label.
conf_fam <- read_table_or_null(
  "study1_confirmatory_family.csv",
  "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.9 (the confirmatory family)",
  stage = "quant")

h1_line <- function(dim) {
  if (is.null(conf_fam)) return(NULL)
  req <- c("hypothesis", "test", "estimate", "se", "df", "statistic",
           "p_raw", "p_holm")
  if (!all(req %in% names(conf_fam))) {
    stop("study1_confirmatory_family.csv is missing expected columns (",
         paste(setdiff(req, names(conf_fam)), collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
         paste(names(conf_fam), collapse = ", "),
         ". Align Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.9 (writer) with this reader.")
  }
  r <- conf_fam %>% filter(hypothesis == "H1", grepl(dim, test, ignore.case = TRUE))
  sprintf(paste0("Human minus machine, estimated marginal contrast averaged ",
                 "over the two image kinds: estimate = %s rating points, ",
                 "SE = %s, t(%s) = %s, p %s; Holm-adjusted p %s"),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$estimate,  paste(dim, "H1 estimate"))),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$se,        paste(dim, "H1 se"))),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$df,        paste(dim, "H1 df")), 1),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$statistic, paste(dim, "H1 statistic"))),
          p_rel(scalar(r$p_raw,     paste(dim, "H1 p_raw"))),
          p_rel(scalar(r$p_holm,    paste(dim, "H1 p_holm"))))
}

# ---- Multiverse summary ------------------------------------------------------
multi_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_specification_curve.csv")
multi <- read_csv(multi_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
record_file("input", multi_path, "read",
            upstream_check(basename(multi_path), "robustness")$note)

# The specification-curve CSV's p-value column is `p`. The required columns
# are checked before use.
multi_req <- c("dimension", "estimate", "p")
if (!all(multi_req %in% names(multi))) {
  stop("study1_specification_curve.csv is missing expected columns (",
       paste(multi_req, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
       paste(names(multi), collapse = ", "),
       ". Re-run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 8 (specification curve).")
}

# What each specification estimates. Every specification fits
# rating ~ Type * stimulus_type within its own model family and reads one
# quantity from the fit. The writer may name that quantity in a column of its
# own (estimand, contrast or quantity). If it does, the line takes the name
# from there, one line per quantity named. If it does not, the quantity is
# the TypeAI coefficient, the machine-minus-human difference at the
# non-figurative image kind, and the line says so. Negative and positive
# estimates are counted separately, under the sign convention the label
# states.
#
# n_estimated counts the specifications with an estimate. n_converged counts
# the TRUE values in the writer's own converged column. Neither count comes
# from model diagnostics computed here, and the line names the column behind
# the second.
multi_quantity_col <- intersect(c("estimand", "contrast", "quantity"),
                                names(multi))[1]
multi <- multi %>%
  mutate(quantity_label = if (is.na(multi_quantity_col)) {
    paste0("TypeAI coefficient, the machine-minus-human difference at the ",
           "non-figurative image kind")
  } else as.character(.data[[multi_quantity_col]]))

multi_summary <- multi %>%
  group_by(dimension, quantity_label) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total       = n(),
    n_estimated   = sum(!is.na(estimate)),
    n_converged   = if ("converged" %in% names(multi))
                      sum(as.logical(converged) %in% TRUE) else NA_integer_,
    n_negative    = sum(estimate < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_positive    = sum(estimate > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_p_below_05  = sum(p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_p      = median(p, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    dimension = stringr::str_to_title(dimension),
    # The sign counts come from the estimates themselves, so a sign flip in
    # any specification shows in the count.
    line = sprintf(paste0("%s, on each family's own scale: %d/%d specifications ",
                          "estimated%s; %d negative and %d positive; %d/%d ",
                          "at p < .05; median p = %.1e"),
                   quantity_label, n_estimated, n_total,
                   ifelse(is.na(n_converged), "",
                          sprintf(", %d recorded as converged in the specification curve's converged column",
                                  n_converged)),
                   n_negative, n_positive,
                   n_p_below_05, n_estimated, median_p)
  )
multiverse_rows <- multi_summary %>%
  transmute(Check = if (dplyr::n_distinct(quantity_label) > 1L)
                      sprintf("Multiverse, %s (%s)", quantity_label, dimension)
                    else sprintf("Multiverse (%s)", dimension),
            Result = line)
stopifnot(nrow(multiverse_rows) >= 2L)

# ---- brms primary (Gaussian) -------------------------------------------------
# The brms CSVs have columns
#   dimension, term, mean, median, ci_lo, ci_hi, pd, rhat, ess_bulk
# and are read by those names.
brms_req <- c("dimension", "term", "mean", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")

brms_p_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_brms_primary_fixed.csv")
brms_p <- read_csv(brms_p_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
record_file("input", brms_p_path, "read",
            upstream_check(basename(brms_p_path), "robustness")$note)
if (!all(brms_req %in% names(brms_p))) {
  stop("study1_brms_primary_fixed.csv is missing expected columns (",
       paste(brms_req, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
       paste(names(brms_p), collapse = ", "),
       ". Re-run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 2.")
}

# Exact term match: a substring match on "TypeAI" would also pick up
# "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure" and return two rows per dimension.
#
# What the TypeAI term is. The model codes image kind with the non-figurative
# level as its reference. TypeAI is therefore the machine-minus-human
# difference at that one level. That makes it a simple effect: the effect of
# attribution within a single level of the other factor, here the
# non-figurative images. The lmerTest TypeAI row of the full fixed-effects
# table (section 7) estimates the same quantity, and the two are compared
# below. The marginal attribution contrast the main text cites is a different
# quantity. It averages the difference over both image kinds, and the two
# coincide only when the interaction is zero.
brms_p_TypeAI <- brms_p %>% filter(term == "TypeAI")
stopifnot(nrow(brms_p_TypeAI) == 2L,
          setequal(brms_p_TypeAI$dimension, c("creativity", "effort")))

# ---- brms cumulative (ordinal) -----------------------------------------------
brms_c_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_brms_cumulative_fixed.csv")
brms_c <- read_csv(brms_c_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
record_file("input", brms_c_path, "read",
            upstream_check(basename(brms_c_path), "robustness")$note)
if (!all(brms_req %in% names(brms_c))) {
  stop("study1_brms_cumulative_fixed.csv is missing expected columns (",
       paste(brms_req, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
       paste(names(brms_c), collapse = ", "),
       ". Re-run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 2.1.")
}
# The cumulative CSV labels dimensions "creativity_cumulative" /
# "effort_cumulative"; the suffix is stripped so the dimension filter below
# matches.
brms_c <- brms_c %>%
  mutate(dimension = sub("_cumulative$", "", dimension))
brms_c_TypeAI <- brms_c %>% filter(term == "TypeAI")
stopifnot(nrow(brms_c_TypeAI) == 2L,
          setequal(brms_c_TypeAI$dimension, c("creativity", "effort")))

# ---- brms-vs-lmerTest agreement ----------------------------------------------
# The agreement is the absolute difference between the posterior mean and the
# lmerTest point estimate of the TypeAI coefficient. The lmerTest estimate is
# read from study1_lmm_fixed_effects.csv.
lmer_fx_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_lmm_fixed_effects.csv")
lmer_fx <- read_csv(lmer_fx_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
record_file("input", lmer_fx_path, "read",
            upstream_check(basename(lmer_fx_path), "quant")$note)
stopifnot(all(c("dimension", "term", "estimate") %in% names(lmer_fx)))
lmer_TypeAI <- lmer_fx %>% filter(term == "TypeAI") %>%
  dplyr::select(dimension, lmer_est = estimate)
stopifnot(nrow(lmer_TypeAI) == 2L)

brms_vs_lmer <- brms_p_TypeAI %>%
  dplyr::select(dimension, brms_mean = mean) %>%
  inner_join(lmer_TypeAI, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(abs_diff = abs(brms_mean - lmer_est))
stopifnot(nrow(brms_vs_lmer) == 2L, !any(is.na(brms_vs_lmer$abs_diff)))

# Row builders. Every extraction passes through scalar(), so a filter that
# matches 0 or 2 rows stops with an error. Each Bayesian cell names its
# quantity: the TypeAI coefficient, the simple effect at the non-figurative
# image kind. That quantity is comparable to the lmerTest TypeAI row, not to
# the marginal contrast the main text cites.
brms_gauss_row <- function(dim) {
  r <- brms_p_TypeAI %>% filter(dimension == dim)
  tol <- brms_vs_lmer %>% filter(dimension == dim) %>% pull(abs_diff)
  sprintf(paste0("TypeAI, the non-figurative simple effect (comparable to the ",
                 "lmerTest TypeAI row, not the marginal contrast in the main ",
                 "text): posterior mean = %s, 95%% CrI [%s, %s]; ",
                 "|posterior mean - lmerTest TypeAI estimate| = %s"),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$mean,  paste(dim, "brms mean"))),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$ci_lo, paste(dim, "brms ci_lo"))),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$ci_hi, paste(dim, "brms ci_hi"))),
          fmt_n(scalar(tol,     paste(dim, "brms-lmer abs diff")), 3))
}
brms_cum_row <- function(dim) {
  r <- brms_c_TypeAI %>% filter(dimension == dim)
  sprintf(paste0("TypeAI, the non-figurative simple effect: posterior mean ",
                 "(logit) = %s, 95%% CrI [%s, %s]"),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$mean,  paste(dim, "cumulative mean"))),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$ci_lo, paste(dim, "cumulative ci_lo"))),
          fmt_n(scalar(r$ci_hi, paste(dim, "cumulative ci_hi"))))
}

# The writer may also deposit a marginal attribution contrast from the
# Bayesian fits, averaged over the two image kinds. Such a row has a term
# containing "marginal", in either brms table, and is reported beside the
# TypeAI rows. The cell quotes the term as the writer names it, because the name
# carries the sign convention. When neither table has such a row, the
# Bayesian rows report the simple effect only, and the caption describes the
# simple effect alone.
brms_marginal_rows <- function(tab, family_label, scale_label) {
  m <- tab %>% filter(grepl("marginal", term, ignore.case = TRUE))
  if (nrow(m) == 0L) return(NULL)
  if (anyNA(m[, c("mean", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")])) {
    stop("A marginal-contrast row of the ", family_label, " brms table has an ",
         "NA mean or interval; re-run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 2.")
  }
  tibble(
    Check  = sprintf("Bayesian replication, %s, marginal contrast (%s)",
                     family_label, stringr::str_to_title(m$dimension)),
    Result = sprintf("%s: posterior mean%s = %s, 95%% CrI [%s, %s]",
                     m$term, scale_label, fmt_n(m$mean), fmt_n(m$ci_lo),
                     fmt_n(m$ci_hi))
  )
}
brms_marginal <- bind_rows(
  brms_marginal_rows(brms_p, "Gaussian", ""),
  brms_marginal_rows(brms_c, "Cumulative-ordinal", " (logit)")
)

# ---- Equivalence at the wider bounds -----------------------------------------
# Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 3 tests the attribution-by-image-kind
# interaction against the wider bounds of 0.30 and 0.50 rating points, as
# descriptive sensitivity. This is not the registered test of H3. That test
# uses the registered bound of +/- 0.20 rating points, runs under both the
# intercepts-only and the maximal random-effects structures, and sits in
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10 with the rest of the confirmatory results.
# The cell built here states this, so a wider bound is not read as the
# registered one.
#
# Column contract from the writer: quantity, dimension, bound,
# bound_is_registered, role, method, source_fit, term, scale, bound_lo,
# bound_hi, estimate, se, df, ci90_lo, ci90_hi, tost_p_low, tost_p_high,
# tost_p, nhst_p, reading, and for the Bayesian rows hdi95_lo, hdi95_hi, pd,
# prop_in_rope_full, prop_in_rope_hdi95.
equiv <- read_table_or_null(
  "study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv",
  "run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 3 (equivalence sensitivity)",
  stage = "robustness")

equivalence_line <- function(dim) {
  if (is.null(equiv)) return(NULL)
  req <- c("dimension", "bound", "method", "estimate", "ci90_lo", "ci90_hi",
           "tost_p", "reading")
  if (!all(req %in% names(equiv))) {
    stop("study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv is missing expected columns (",
         paste(setdiff(req, names(equiv)), collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
         paste(names(equiv), collapse = ", "),
         ". Align Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 3 (writer) with this reader.")
  }
  t <- equiv %>%
    filter(dimension == dim, grepl("^two one-sided", method)) %>%
    arrange(bound)
  if (nrow(t) == 0L) {
    stop("No two-one-sided-test rows for dimension '", dim,
         "' in study1_equivalence_sensitivity.csv; re-run ",
         "Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 3.")
  }
  if (anyNA(t[, req[req != "method"]])) {
    stop("Equivalence sensitivity rows for dimension '", dim,
         "' carry NA values; re-run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 3.")
  }
  # The estimate is the same at every bound; only the bound moves.
  stopifnot(diff(range(t$estimate)) < 1e-8)
  # fmt_p() returns either a number or the string "< 0.001". The relation
  # sign is therefore chosen here. Typed into the sentence, it would read
  # "p = < 0.001" for the small p-values.
  p_phrase <- ifelse(t$tost_p < 0.001,
                     "larger one-sided p < 0.001",
                     sprintf("larger one-sided p = %s", fmt_p(t$tost_p)))
  per_bound <- sprintf("bound +/- %.2f: %s (%s)",
                       t$bound, t$reading, p_phrase)
  sprintf(paste0("Interaction estimate = %s rating points, 90%% CI [%s, %s]. ",
                 "%s. Descriptive sensitivity only; the registered test of H3 ",
                 "at +/- 0.20 rating points, under both random-effects ",
                 "structures, is in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10."),
          fmt_n(t$estimate[1]), fmt_n(t$ci90_lo[1]), fmt_n(t$ci90_hi[1]),
          paste(per_bound, collapse = "; "))
}

# ---- Build the combined robustness table ------------------------------------
# Rows are assembled one at a time. A row whose guarded source table is
# absent is left out, so the table gets shorter and the knit goes on. The
# Check label of every row names the quantity it reports.
robustness_rows <- bind_rows(
  if (!is.null(conf_fam))
    tibble(Check = "Registered H1 contrast (Creativity)",
           Result = h1_line("creativity")),
  if (!is.null(conf_fam))
    tibble(Check = "Registered H1 contrast (Effort)",
           Result = h1_line("effort")),
  multiverse_rows,
  tibble(Check = "Bayesian replication, Gaussian, TypeAI simple effect (Creativity)",
         Result = brms_gauss_row("creativity")),
  tibble(Check = "Bayesian replication, Gaussian, TypeAI simple effect (Effort)",
         Result = brms_gauss_row("effort")),
  tibble(Check = "Bayesian replication, Cumulative-ordinal, TypeAI simple effect (Creativity)",
         Result = brms_cum_row("creativity")),
  tibble(Check = "Bayesian replication, Cumulative-ordinal, TypeAI simple effect (Effort)",
         Result = brms_cum_row("effort")),
  brms_marginal,
  if (!is.null(equiv))
    tibble(Check = "Equivalence sensitivity, attribution-by-image-kind interaction (Creativity)",
           Result = equivalence_line("creativity")),
  if (!is.null(equiv))
    tibble(Check = "Equivalence sensitivity, attribution-by-image-kind interaction (Effort)",
           Result = equivalence_line("effort"))
)
stopifnot(nrow(robustness_rows) >= 6L, !any(is.na(robustness_rows$Result)))

# The caption names the quantity behind each kind of row. Its sentences on
# the H1 rows, the multiverse and a Bayesian marginal row follow what the
# tables on disk carry, so the caption never describes an absent row.
supp1_caption <- paste0(
  "Robustness checks for the Study 1 attribution effect. Every entry is ",
  "computed from the pipeline output tables (the confirmatory family, the ",
  "specification curve, the brms fixed-effect summaries, the lmerTest ",
  "coefficients, and the equivalence sensitivity table); no cell is typed by ",
  "hand. ",
  if (!is.null(conf_fam)) paste0(
    "The two H1 rows are the registered quantity the main text cites: the ",
    "Human-minus-machine difference in mean rating, estimated from each ",
    "dimension's primary mixed model and averaged with equal weight over the ",
    "two image kinds, with its p-value before and after the Holm correction ",
    "across the confirmatory family. Every other row reports a related but ",
    "different quantity, which its label names. ")
  else paste0(
    "The registered H1 rows are left out because the confirmatory family ",
    "table is not on disk. Every row reports a quantity related to H1 but ",
    "different from it, which its label names. "),
  if (is.na(multi_quantity_col)) paste0(
    "The multiverse rows summarise the specification curve, in which each ",
    "specification fits the rating on attribution, image kind and their ",
    "interaction within its own model family and reads the TypeAI ",
    "coefficient, the machine-minus-human ",
    "difference at the non-figurative image kind, on that family's own scale ",
    "(rating points, or log-odds for the ordinal family); a negative estimate ",
    "means lower ratings under machine attribution. Estimated counts the ",
    "specifications with an estimate; converged is the specification curve's own record, ",
    "not a diagnostic computed for this table. ")
  else paste0(
    "The multiverse rows summarise the specification curve, one row per ",
    "quantity the specification curve names in its ", multi_quantity_col, " column, on ",
    "each model family's own scale (rating points, or log-odds for the ",
    "ordinal family). Estimated counts the specifications with an estimate; ",
    "converged is the specification curve's own record, not a diagnostic computed for this table. "),
  "The TypeAI rows of the Bayesian replication report the machine-minus-human ",
  "difference at the non-figurative image kind, the reference level of the ",
  "image-kind factor: a simple effect, meaning the effect of attribution ",
  "within one level of the other factor. It is the same quantity as the ",
  "lmerTest TypeAI row of the full fixed-effects table and is compared with ",
  "it; it coincides with the H1 contrast only when the attribution-by-image-",
  "kind interaction is zero, and its sign runs the other way, a negative ",
  "value meaning lower ratings under machine attribution. ",
  if (!is.null(brms_marginal) && nrow(brms_marginal) > 0L)
    paste0("The marginal-contrast rows of the Bayesian replication average ",
           "the difference over the two image kinds, as H1 does, with the sign ",
           "convention the quoted term states. ")
  else "",
  "CrI is the credible interval, the range holding 95\\% of the posterior. ",
  "The equivalence rows concern the attribution-by-image-kind interaction, ",
  "the quantity of H3 rather than of H1, at the wider bounds of 0.30 and ",
  "0.50 rating points, and carry no verdict on H3."
)

robustness_rows %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format    = "latex",
    booktabs  = TRUE,
    caption   = supp1_caption,
    label     = "supp_table_1"
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                            font_size = 9) %>%
  kableExtra::column_spec(2, width = "10cm") %>%
  write_fragment("sup_table_1_robustness.tex")

robustness_rows
```

# 5. Supplementary Table 2: Rates in the written justifications

Each participant wrote a short explanation after every rating. The
explanations are measured by fixed search patterns: lists of words and
phrases, applied the same way to every response and published in full beside
the analysis. `Study1_03_Integration.Rmd` reports how often each pattern
fires. Its interval comes from resampling participants, not responses,
because the participant is the unit that varies.

The table below gives those rates for the arm told a person made the work.
"Effort" has three candidate meanings here: visible detail in the picture,
elapsed time, and skill and training. "Creativity" has three as well: the
idea behind the work, whether it looks familiar, and how finely it is
executed. The rates are read from the pipeline tables, not recomputed here,
so the supplement and the main text report the same numbers.

```{r supp-table-2}
remove_fragment("sup_table_2_text_rates.tex")
prev_effort <- read_table_or_null(
  "study1_text_effort_prevalence.csv",
  "run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd section 3.1 (effort-talk prevalence)",
  stage = "integration")
prev_creat <- read_table_or_null(
  "study1_text_creativity_prevalence.csv",
  "run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd section 4.1 (creativity-talk prevalence)",
  stage = "integration")

if (is.null(prev_effort) && is.null(prev_creat)) {
  cat("Supplementary Table 2 not written: neither prevalence table is on disk.\n")
  record_file("output", file.path(PATH_SUP_TAB, "sup_table_2_text_rates.tex"),
              "pending", "neither prevalence table is on disk")
} else {
  prev_req <- c("quantity", "estimate", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")
  check_prev <- function(d, nm) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    if (!all(prev_req %in% names(d))) {
      stop(nm, " is missing expected columns (",
           paste(prev_req, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
           paste(names(d), collapse = ", "),
           ". Align Study1_03_Integration.Rmd (writer) with this reader.")
    }
    d
  }
  prev_effort <- check_prev(prev_effort, "study1_text_effort_prevalence.csv")
  prev_creat  <- check_prev(prev_creat,  "study1_text_creativity_prevalence.csv")

  # Plain-language names for the quantities, so a reader of the typeset table
  # need not decode a name such as "novelty_either".
  quantity_labels <- c(
    detail            = "Visible detail in the picture",
    time              = "Time and industriousness",
    skill             = "Skill and training",
    none_of_the_three = "None of the three",
    concept           = "The idea behind the work",
    novelty_asserted  = "Says the work looks familiar",
    novelty_negated   = "Says the work does not look familiar",
    novelty_either    = "Raises familiarity either way",
    execution         = "Visible detail and rendering"
  )

  text_rates <- bind_rows(prev_effort, prev_creat) %>%
    mutate(
      Question = stringr::str_to_title(as.character(dimension)),
      Measure  = dplyr::coalesce(unname(quantity_labels[quantity]), quantity),
      Rate     = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * estimate),
      `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.1f%%, %.1f%%]", 100 * ci_lo, 100 * ci_hi)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Question, Measure, Rate, `95% CI`)
  stopifnot(nrow(text_rates) > 0L, !any(is.na(text_rates$Rate)))

  text_rates %>%
    knitr::kable(
      format    = "latex",
      booktabs  = TRUE,
      caption   = "Rates in the written justifications of the human-attribution arm: how often each fixed search pattern fired, as a share of justifications, with a 95\\% interval from resampling participants. The categories are not mutually exclusive, since one sentence can mention detail and time, so the rates need not sum to 100\\%; the share mentioning none of the three is reported beside them.",
      label     = "supp_table_2"
    ) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                              font_size = 9) %>%
    write_fragment("sup_table_2_text_rates.tex")

  text_rates
}
```

# 6. Supplementary Table 3: Prompting and generating talk, by arm

The same prompting-and-generating pattern is counted in both arms. In the arm
told an image generator made the work, the pattern describes what those
participants were told. In the arm told a person made the work, it records
how often an explanation mentions a machine, a prompt or a generated image.
A mention is not the same as rejecting the account of the work the
participant was given. An explanation can mention a machine to compare, to
deny or to wonder. The belief audit in `Study1_03_Integration.Rmd` reports
two counts of human-arm participants. Both come from fixed search patterns
applied the same way to every response, and no person reads or judges any
response. The broad count takes a participant whose explanations mention any
machine, prompting or generating word. The narrow count takes a participant
with at least one explanation that states the work is machine-made. That
means a phrase naming a machine as the maker of the work, with no negating
word inside the phrase or earlier in the same clause ("doesn't look AI
generated"), in a clause not opened by a conditional ("if a computer made
this"). A hedged impression such as "looks AI generated" counts as stating
it. Neither count says whether a participant accepted the account of the
work they were given.

```{r supp-table-3}
# Rendered as the producing notebook writes it: one row per arm, with the rate
# and a participant-resampled interval.
render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_text_prompt_by_arm.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_3_prompt_talk.tex",
  caption     = "Prompting-and-generating talk in the effort justifications of each arm: the share of justifications whose text mentions a machine, a prompt or a generated image, with a 95\\% interval from resampling participants. In the machine-attribution arm this is description of what participants were told. In the human-attribution arm it is the rate at which an explanation mentions a machine, which is not the same as rejecting the account of the work, since a mention can compare, deny or wonder. The belief audit reports two counts of human-arm participants, both from fixed search patterns with no response read or judged by a person: the broad count, of participants whose explanations mention any machine, prompting or generating word, and the narrow count, of participants with at least one explanation that states the work is machine-made, meaning a phrase naming a machine as maker that is neither negated nor inside a conditional (a hedged impression such as looks AI generated counts as stating it).",
  label       = "supp_table_3",
  pending_msg = "run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd section 6 (prompting talk by arm)",
  stage       = "integration"
)
```

# 7. Full LMM regression table (extra supplementary)

```{r supp-table-full-lmm}
remove_fragment("sup_table_full_lmm.tex")
creat_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_creativity.rds")
eff_path   <- file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_effort.rds")
creat_res  <- readRDS(creat_path)
eff_res    <- readRDS(eff_path)
record_file("input", creat_path, "read",
            upstream_check(basename(creat_path), "quant")$note)
record_file("input", eff_path, "read",
            upstream_check(basename(eff_path), "quant")$note)

tidy_creat <- broom.mixed::tidy(creat_res$fit, effects = "fixed",
                                conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(DV = "Creativity")
tidy_eff <- broom.mixed::tidy(eff_res$fit, effects = "fixed",
                              conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(DV = "Effort")

tidy_combined <- bind_rows(tidy_creat, tidy_eff) %>%
  mutate(
    `b (SE)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", estimate, std.error),

  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(DV, term, `b (SE)`, `95% CI`, p)

tidy_combined %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format    = "latex",
    booktabs  = TRUE,
    caption   = "Full fixed-effects estimates from the linear mixed-effects models for creativity and effort. Random effects: participant and stimulus image intercepts. Image kind is coded with the non-figurative images as the reference level, so TypeAI is the machine-minus-human difference at the non-figurative image kind, a simple effect; the H1 contrast, averaged over the two image kinds, is the first pair of rows of Supplementary Table 1.",
    label     = "supp_lmm"
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                            font_size = 9) %>%
  kableExtra::collapse_rows(columns = 1, latex_hline = "major") %>%
  write_fragment("sup_table_full_lmm.tex")

tidy_combined
```

```{r supp-fig-1}
# Source PDFs in the analysis figures folder, written by chunk
# `spec-curve-plot` in Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd:

# Each is copied unchanged into supplement/figures under its Supplementary
# Figure name. The copies from an earlier knit are deleted first, so a

src_eff   <- file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_specification_curve_effort.pdf")

}
```

# 10. Registered completion-set tables

These tables render the CSVs that `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd` writes and, for the
written explanations, the CSVs that `Study1_03_Integration.Rmd` writes. They
cover the quantities the preregistration commits to reporting:

- the joint attribution × dimension model;
- the maximal random-effects model;
- covariate balance and differential attrition;
- the registered bootstrap Cohen's *d*;
- leave-one-participant-out and leave-one-stimulus-out influence;
- the H4 variance test, with its two ratios and their intervals;
- the Holm correction across the confirmatory family;
- H2 in its raw-scale and ordinal versions;
- the sampling spread of the H4 ratio estimate at this design's arm sizes;
- the five registered tests on the written explanations, with their
  Benjamini-Hochberg correction (a correction that limits the expected share
  of false positives among the tests called significant), and their refit
  with a participant random slope;
- the registered test of H3 under both random-effects structures;
- the two checks run in every study where the rating exists: how far the
  rating and the arm can be recovered from the words, and within-person word
  overlap by arm.

Each table is guarded. Its chunk first deletes the table's `.tex` fragment.
If the source CSV has not been produced, or the producing stage's run
manifest lists it as not written, the chunk prints a `pending:` message
naming the notebook that writes it, and it writes nothing. A fragment on disk
was therefore written by the latest knit, from the table on disk at the
time. `tables/study1_supplements_run_manifest.csv` records which table, by
its fingerprint.


## 10.1 Joint Type × dimension model

```{r supp-table-joint-model}
# The joint model, rating ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type as specified in
# Study1_01_Quant.Rmd, tests whether the Type effect differs between
# creativity and effort. The main text makes the same cross-dimension
# comparison descriptively.
# Column contract from the writer code in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.6:
# as.data.frame(anova) with the row names moved to `term`, giving term,
# Sum Sq, Mean Sq, NumDF, DenDF, F value, Pr(>F). The table is rendered as
# deposited, with Pr(>F) formatted by fmt_p().
render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_joint_model_anova.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_joint_model.tex",
  caption     = "Joint mixed model with dimension (creativity vs effort) as a within-participant factor: Type III ANOVA (Satterthwaite). The Type x dimension term tests whether the source-attribution penalty differs across judgment dimensions.",
  label       = "supp_joint_model",
  pending_msg = "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.6 (joint Type x dimension model)",
  stage       = "quant"
)
```

Beside it, d\\_model\\_based is the estimated marginal attribution contrast divided by the square root of the summed variance components of the primary model, which puts the effect on the scale of a single rating rather than of a ten-rating average and is the value comparable to between-subject effect sizes reported elsewhere. ## 10.6 Influence: leave-one-participant-out and leave-one-stimulus-out

```{r supp-table-influence}
# Summarise the LOPO and LOSO refit tables (leave-one-participant-out and
# leave-one-stimulus-out) to the largest and the mean absolute change in the
# tracked estimate, per dimension. The change is the writer's delta column:
# the estimate from the refit with one participant or one image left out,
# minus the same estimate from the full sample. The raw per-refit CSVs (111 +
# 10 rows per dimension) are too long to typeset.
# Column contract from the writer code in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.7:
# dimension, unit, dropped, estimate, se, est_full, delta (= estimate -
# est_full), converged, singular, fit_error, note, quantity. The quantity
# column names the tracked estimate on every row. It is the registered H1
# contrast: the Human-minus-machine difference in mean rating, averaged with
# equal weight over the two image kinds. The column headers below name that
# contrast, so the chunk stops if the quantity column is absent or names
# anything else, and prints the columns or values it found. A refit that
# errored or did not converge carries no estimate and an NA delta. The
# largest and mean changes are taken over the usable refits, and the table
# counts them.
influence_cols <- c(
  largest = "Largest absolute change in the H1 contrast",
  mean    = "Mean absolute change in the H1 contrast"
)

summarise_influence <- function(df, unit_label) {
  req <- c("dimension", "delta", "quantity")
  if (!all(req %in% names(df))) {
    stop("Influence CSV (", unit_label, ") lacks ",
         paste(setdiff(req, names(df)), collapse = ", "), ". Found: ",
         paste(names(df), collapse = ", "),
         ". Expected the columns written by Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.7.")
  }
  q <- unique(df$quantity)
  if (length(q) != 1L || is.na(q) || !grepl("^H1", q)) {
    stop("Influence CSV (", unit_label, ") tracks: ",
         paste(q, collapse = "; "), ". The column headers of this table name ",
         "the H1 contrast, so they would misname this quantity.")
  }
  df %>%
    group_by(dimension) %>%
    summarise(
      Refits          = n(),
      `Usable refits` = sum(!is.na(delta)),
      largest         = max(abs(delta), na.rm = TRUE),
      mean            = mean(abs(delta), na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    rename(all_of(setNames(names(influence_cols), influence_cols))) %>%
    mutate(`Left out` = unit_label, .before = 1)
}

remove_fragment("sup_table_influence.tex")
influence_pending <- "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.7 (LOPO/LOSO influence)"
lopo <- read_table_or_null("study1_influence_lopo.csv", influence_pending,
                           stage = "quant")
loso <- read_table_or_null("study1_influence_loso.csv", influence_pending,
                           stage = "quant")

if (!is.null(lopo) && !is.null(loso)) {
  influence_summary <- bind_rows(
    summarise_influence(lopo, "Participant (LOPO)"),
    summarise_influence(loso, "Stimulus (LOSO)")
  ) %>%
    mutate(dimension = stringr::str_to_title(dimension)) %>%
    rename(Dimension = dimension)
  stopifnot(nrow(influence_summary) >= 4L,
            !any(is.na(influence_summary[[influence_cols[["largest"]]]])))

  influence_caption <- paste0(
    "Influence diagnostics for the registered H1 contrast, the ",
    "Human-minus-machine difference in mean rating averaged with equal ",
    "weight over the two image kinds. Each participant (LOPO) or each ",
    "stimulus image (LOSO) is left out in turn and the primary model is ",
    "refit. The table gives, per dimension, the largest and the mean ",
    "absolute change in the contrast from its full-sample value, in rating ",
    "points, over the usable refits: those that converged without error.",
    writer_quote(tibble(quantity = c(lopo$quantity, loso$quantity)),
                 "quantity", "The quantity as Study1\\_01\\_Quant.Rmd names it"),
    " The estimate of each refit is deposited as ",
    "tables/study1\\_influence\\_lopo.csv and ",
    "tables/study1\\_influence\\_loso.csv."
  )

  influence_tex <- influence_summary %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(unname(influence_cols)), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      format   = "latex",
      booktabs = TRUE,
      caption  = influence_caption,
      label    = "supp_influence"
    ) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                              font_size = 9)
  # The two long headers are set at a fixed width, so they wrap onto two
  # lines and the table fits the page.
  for (nm in unname(influence_cols)) {
    influence_tex <- kableExtra::column_spec(
      influence_tex, which(names(influence_summary) == nm), width = "2.8cm")
  }
  write_fragment(influence_tex, "sup_table_influence.tex")
  influence_summary
} else {
  record_file("output", file.path(PATH_SUP_TAB, "sup_table_influence.tex"),
              "pending", influence_pending)
}
```


## 10.7 H4: the registered variance test

```{r supp-table-h4-variance}
# H4 predicts that attribution changes what a rating is a property of. Under
# machine attribution a rating should reflect the person judging more and the
# particular artwork less. Two ratios are read, each on the absolute variance
# scale and not as a share of the total, and each with an interval. One is
# the machine-to-human ratio of between-participant variance. The other is
# the machine-to-human ratio of residual variance. Shares are compositional:
# when one component shrinks, the others rise arithmetically. A shift in
# shares is therefore not by itself evidence of the structural change H4
# asserts.
#
# The two ratios come from two fits with different residual structures. The
# between-participant ratio is read from a crossed mixed model (lme4) with a
# participant intercept whose variance may differ by arm, an image intercept,
# and one residual variance shared by the two arms. Its likelihood ratio test
# (a comparison of how well two nested models fit the data) compares that
# model with one holding the participant variance common to both arms. The
# residual ratio is read from a second model (nlme). In it the participant
# variance and the residual variance both differ by arm, but there is no
# image intercept. Its residual stratum therefore also holds the differences
# between images that image kind does not explain. Its likelihood ratio test
# compares it with the same model holding one residual variance. The two
# ratios do not partition one fitted variance structure, and the caption says
# so.
#
# The reference distribution of the deposited test. Two candidates are easy
# to confuse. A boundary-corrected mixture, half a chi-square and half a spike
# at zero, is the right reference when a variance is tested against zero. A
# variance cannot be negative, so that null value sits at the edge of the
# parameter's range. That is not this test. The registered comparison sets two
# variances equal to each other, both estimated as positive. That is an
# interior point of the parameter space, so the ordinary chi-square on one
# degree of freedom is the correct reference, and Study1_01_Quant.Rmd
# section 7.8 computes that one. The deposited table states its
# reference in its own `lrt_between_reference` column, so the file does not
# depend on this caption for it.
#
# How each ratio gets its interval. A ratio of two estimated variances has no
```
