```{r supp-table-h4-variance}
# simple closed-form interval. Each ratio is therefore bootstrapped at the
# level of the participant, the unit that was randomised to an arm.
# Participants are resampled with replacement within each arm, so the two arm
# sizes stay fixed. A participant drawn twice is relabelled as two distinct
# ids. A random-effects model given the same id twice would treat the copies
# as one person and misestimate the participant variance. Both fits (the lme4
# model with arm-specific participant variances and the nlme model with
# arm-specific residual variances) are refit on every resample. The interval
# on each ratio runs from the 2.5th to the 97.5th percentile of the resampled
# ratios. A refit that fails, or that is singular, is counted. Singular here
# means the optimiser pushed one of the estimated variances to zero, the edge
# of its range. The deposited file carries the interval columns
# ci_low_between, ci_high_between, ci_low_residual, ci_high_residual; the
# resample count n_boot; the failure and singularity counts
# n_boot_failed_between, n_boot_failed_residual, n_boot_singular_between; and
# h4_supported. h4_supported is the registered conjunction in one column: the
# participant ratio's interval lies wholly above 1 and the residual ratio's
# wholly below 1.
#
# Column contract: Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.8 writes the file read here.
# It carries the ratios and the likelihood ratio tests, not the descriptive
# three-way partition that sits beside it. The typeset table keeps the
# columns a reader needs to check the claim: the dimension, each ratio with
# its interval, the two likelihood ratio statistics with their p-values, and
# h4_supported. The two reference columns are one sentence each, repeated on
# every row, and drop_long_constant_columns() prints them once above the
# table. The arm-specific variances, the resample count and the failure and
# singularity counts stay in the deposited CSV, which the caption points to.
# If none of the kept columns is present, the file is rendered whole, less
# the constant text.
h4_var_keep <- c("dimension",
                 "ratio_between_AI_over_Human", "ci_low_between",
                 "ci_high_between",
                 "ratio_residual_AI_over_Human", "ci_low_residual",
                 "ci_high_residual",
                 "lrt_between_chisq", "lrt_between_p",
                 "lrt_residual_chisq", "lrt_residual_p",
                 "h4_supported")
render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_h4_variance_test.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_h4_variance.tex",
  caption     = "H4, the registered variance test by attribution arm: the ratio of machine-arm to human-arm between-participant variance and the ratio of machine-arm to human-arm residual variance, both on the absolute variance scale; with the likelihood ratio test of each against a model holding that variance common to the two arms (lrt\\_between\\_chisq and lrt\\_between\\_p for the between-participant variance, lrt\\_residual\\_chisq and lrt\\_residual\\_p for the residual variance). The two ratios come from two fits with different residual structures. The between-participant ratio is from a crossed mixed model with participant and image intercepts, the participant variance free by arm and one residual variance shared by the arms. The residual ratio is from a second model in which the participant and the residual variances both differ by arm but which has no image intercept, so its residual also holds the differences between images that image kind does not explain. Each test sets two positive variances equal, an interior point of the parameter space, so it is referred to an ordinary chi-square on one degree of freedom rather than to a boundary-corrected mixture; the deposited file records this in its own reference columns. Each ratio carries a 95\\% interval from a participant-level percentile bootstrap, in which participants are resampled with replacement within each arm, duplicated participants are relabelled as distinct so the random-effects fit stays valid, both models are refit on every resample, and the interval is read from the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the resampled ratios. H4 is supported on a dimension only if the participant ratio's interval lies wholly above 1 and the residual ratio's wholly below 1, a conjunction the h4\\_supported column states, and H4 as registered requires it on both dimensions. This table shows the ratios, their intervals, the two tests and that verdict; the full table, with the arm-specific variances, the reference distribution of each test, the resample count, and the number of resamples whose refit failed or was singular, is deposited as tables/study1\\_h4\\_variance\\_test.csv.",
  label       = "supp_h4_variance",
  pending_msg = "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.8 (the registered H4 variance test)",
  transform   = function(df) {
    df <- drop_long_constant_columns(df)
    if (any(h4_var_keep %in% names(df))) {
      df <- df %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(h4_var_keep))
    }
    df
  },
  stage       = "quant"
)
```

## 10.8 The confirmatory family and its Holm correction

```{r supp-table-holm-family}
# The preregistration lists the confirmatory family: the attribution contrast
# on creativity, the attribution contrast on effort, the
# attribution-by-dimension contrast, and the H4 variance-ratio test. Those
# four p-values are corrected together by the Holm procedure at a family-wise
# alpha of .05. Holm orders the tests from the smallest p-value upward and
# compares each against a threshold that starts strictest and relaxes as
# earlier tests pass. This table is the record of that correction. It should
# show the four tests, their raw p-values, the order they were placed in, the
# threshold each met or failed, and the adjusted value.
#
# Two points govern how the table is read. H1 is a conjunction: it requires
# the effect on both dimensions. Correcting its two parts alongside the other
# tests is therefore conservative, and that cost is accepted. H3 is not in
# this family. It is a prediction of no effect, decided by the equivalence
# procedure and its four-cell table, not by a corrected p-value.
#
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.9):
# hypothesis, test, estimate, se, df, statistic, statistic_type, p_raw,
# p_holm, survives_holm_at_05, family_size, correction, h4_creativity_lrt_p,
# h4_effort_lrt_p, fits_converged, note. The two H4 columns are the
# likelihood ratio p-values on each dimension, and the weaker of the two
# enters the family.
#
# Typeset whole, the table is too wide for the page. The typeset table keeps
# the columns a reader needs to check the correction: the hypothesis and the
# test, the estimate with its precision, the statistic with its type, the raw
# and Holm-adjusted p-values, and survives_holm_at_05, the verdict. The
# precision is the interval when the writer deposits one, and the standard
# error otherwise; the caption says which. keep_columns_report()
# prints every other column once on the console, beside the hypothesis and
# the test, and the caption points to the deposited CSV for them. The test
# column holds a sentence on every row and is set at a fixed width, so it
# wraps.
holm_interval_cols <- function(df) {
  pairs <- list(c("ci_low", "ci_high"), c("ci_lo", "ci_hi"),
                c("conf.low", "conf.high"))
  hit <- Filter(function(p) all(p %in% names(df)), pairs)
  if (length(hit) > 0L) hit[[1]] else character(0)
}
holm_keep <- function(df) {
  precision <- holm_interval_cols(df)
  if (length(precision) == 0L) precision <- "se"
  c("hypothesis", "test", "estimate", precision, "statistic_type",
    "statistic", "p_raw", "p_holm", "survives_holm_at_05")
}
#
# The H4 row of the family is only the between-participant half of H4: the
# likelihood ratio test of letting the between-participant variance differ by
# arm. A pass on that row does not establish H4. H4 also requires lower
# residual variance under machine attribution, with each ratio's interval on
# the predicted side of 1, on both dimensions. That full criterion is the
# h4_supported column of the H4 variance table (section 10.7). When that
# table is on disk, the caption reads h4_supported from it and states on
# which dimensions the full criterion holds. The per-dimension verdict then
# sits beside the family's row.
h4_full <- read_table_or_null(
  "study1_h4_variance_test.csv",
  "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.8 (the registered H4 variance test)",
  stage = "quant")
h4_full_sentence <- if (!is.null(h4_full) &&
                        all(c("dimension", "h4_supported") %in% names(h4_full))) {
  met     <- as.logical(h4_full$h4_supported)
  dims_ok <- h4_full$dimension[met %in% TRUE]
  dims_no <- h4_full$dimension[met %in% FALSE]
  both    <- length(dims_ok) == 2L && length(dims_no) == 0L
  cat("Full H4 criterion (h4_supported) holds on: ",
      if (length(dims_ok)) paste(dims_ok, collapse = ", ") else "neither dimension",
      "; does not hold on: ",
      if (length(dims_no)) paste(dims_no, collapse = ", ") else "neither dimension",
      ". H4 as registered, on both dimensions: ",
      if (both) "supported" else "not supported", ".\n", sep = "")
  paste0(
    " In the H4 variance table the full criterion holds on ",
    if (length(dims_ok)) paste(dims_ok, collapse = " and ") else "neither dimension",
    if (length(dims_no)) paste0(" and does not hold on ",
                                paste(dims_no, collapse = " and ")) else "",
    ", so H4 as registered, which requires both dimensions, is ",
    if (both) "supported." else "not supported."
  )
} else ""

holm_caption <- function(df) {
  precision <- if (length(holm_interval_cols(df)) > 0L)
    paste0("its interval (", latex_escape(paste(holm_interval_cols(df),
                                                collapse = ", ")), ")")
  else "its standard error (se)"
  no_interval <- if (length(holm_interval_cols(df)) == 0L)
    " The deposited table carries no interval for the family." else ""
  paste0("The confirmatory family and its Holm correction: the attribution contrast on creativity, the attribution contrast on effort, the attribution-by-dimension contrast, and the H4 variance-ratio test, with raw and Holm-adjusted p-values at a family-wise alpha of .05 (the Holm procedure orders the tests from the smallest p-value upward and compares each against a threshold that starts strictest and relaxes as earlier tests pass). The two attribution contrasts are the Human-minus-machine difference averaged with equal weight over the two image kinds. The H4 row is the between-participant half of H4 only, the likelihood ratio test of letting the between-participant variance differ by arm, at the weaker of the two dimensions. A surviving H4 row does not establish H4, which also requires lower residual variance under machine attribution, with each ratio's interval on the predicted side of 1, on both dimensions: the h4\\_supported column of the H4 variance table.", h4_full_sentence, " H3 is not part of this family: it is a null prediction, decided by the equivalence procedure. Any false-discovery-rate column elsewhere in these tables is descriptive and is not this correction. Each row shows the estimate with ", precision, ", the test statistic with its type (statistic\\_type), the raw and the Holm-adjusted p-values (p\\_raw, p\\_holm), and whether the test survives the correction (survives\\_holm\\_at\\_05).", no_interval, " The estimate of the H4 row is the machine-to-human ratio of between-participant variance, which has no standard error here; its bootstrap interval is in the H4 variance table. The full table, with the degrees of freedom, the family size, the wording of the correction, the H4 likelihood ratio p-value on each dimension, whether the fits converged and a note on each row, is deposited as tables/study1\\_confirmatory\\_family.csv.")
}

render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_confirmatory_family.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_holm_family.tex",
  caption     = holm_caption,
  label       = "supp_holm_family",
  pending_msg = "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd (Holm correction across the confirmatory family)",
  transform   = function(df) keep_columns_report(
    df, keep = holm_keep(df), key = c("hypothesis", "test")),
  stage       = "quant",
  col_widths  = c(test = "5cm")
)
```

## 10.9 H2 in its two registered versions: raw scale and ordinal

H2 says the attribution penalty is larger on effort than on creativity. The
preregistration registers two versions of that test, because the two
dimensions need not start at the same level under human attribution. A
rating further from the floor of a five-point scale has more room to fall.
The first version
is the raw-scale attribution-by-dimension contrast from the joint model of
section 10.1, in rating points. The second is the same contrast in a
cumulative-link mixed model. That model treats the five response options as
ordered categories cut from one underlying continuous scale, not as equally
spaced numbers. Crowding near the floor is then absorbed by the category
thresholds and not by the effect. H2 is claimed only if the two versions
agree in sign and in significance. A disagreement is reported as a failure
of H2, with the range explanation named: that the two dimensions had
different room to fall.

```{r supp-table-h2-ordinal}
# The ordinal model is fitted on the stacked response, both dimensions in one
# frame, as Type * dimension * stimulus_type with random structure
# (1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension). The by-participant slope
# for dimension lets each person's own effort-minus-creativity gap vary, and
# the interaction is tested against that variation. The second term gives one
# intercept per image-by-dimension cell. When the slope structure does not
# converge, the registered fallback is (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension).
# The table's random_structure_used column records which was fitted, so a
# reduced structure is labelled as reduced.
#
# Column contract from the writer: version, scale, estimate, SE, df,
# statistic, statistic_type, p, sign, significant_at_05,
# random_structure_used, converged, max_abs_gradient,
# agree_sign_and_significance, definition. One row per version. The ordinal
# estimate is on that model's log-odds scale and the raw-scale estimate is in
# rating points, so the two are compared on sign and significance, never on
# size.
#
# Two columns are handled before formatting. The first is df. The raw-scale
# statistic is a t with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, an approximation to
# the degrees of freedom of a test in a mixed model. The ordinal statistic is
# a z, referred to the standard normal distribution, and the writer records
# its df as infinite. That cell is typeset as "normal reference", not as the
# word Inf. The second is the definition of the contrast, one sentence
# repeated on both rows, which drop_long_constant_columns() prints once above
# the table. random_structure_used is also the same on both rows, but the
# caption names it and the code below reads it, so it is kept.
h2_ordinal <- render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_h2_ordinal.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_h2_ordinal.tex",
  caption     = "H2 in its two registered versions. The raw-scale row is the attribution-by-dimension contrast from the joint mixed model, in rating points; the ordinal row is the same contrast from a cumulative-link mixed model, which treats the five response options as ordered categories cut from one underlying continuous scale rather than as equally spaced numbers, so that crowding near the floor is absorbed by the category thresholds rather than by the effect, and its estimate is on that model's log-odds scale. The raw-scale statistic is a t with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; the ordinal statistic is a z referred to the standard normal distribution, so its df cell reads normal reference rather than a number. Both are fitted on the stacked response with a by-participant slope for dimension and one intercept per image-by-dimension cell; the random\\_structure\\_used column records whether the registered fallback to a participant intercept only was needed, and converged records whether the fit finished cleanly. H2 is claimed only if the two rows agree in sign and in significance, which the final column states.",
  label       = "supp_h2_ordinal",
  pending_msg = "run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd (H2 in the cumulative-link mixed model, beside the joint model of section 7.6)",
  transform   = function(df) {
    df <- drop_long_constant_columns(df, keep = "random_structure_used")
    if ("df" %in% names(df) && is.numeric(df$df)) {
      df <- df %>%
        mutate(df = ifelse(is.infinite(df), "normal reference",
                           fmt_n(df, 3)))
    }
    df
  },
  stage       = "quant"
)

# The random structure of each version, and the registered decision, are
# also printed in words. A fallback to the intercept-only structure is then
# stated outright and need not be decoded from a column.
if (!is.null(h2_ordinal)) {
  h2_req <- c("version", "random_structure_used", "converged",
              "agree_sign_and_significance")
  if (!all(h2_req %in% names(h2_ordinal))) {
    stop("study1_h2_ordinal.csv is missing expected columns (",
         paste(setdiff(h2_req, names(h2_ordinal)), collapse = ", "),
         "). Found: ", paste(names(h2_ordinal), collapse = ", "),
         ". Align the writer in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd with this reader.")
  }
  # The registered structure carries a by-participant slope for dimension.
  # The recorded formula is matched against that slope first and against the
  # intercept-only fallback second. A formula that matches neither is quoted
  # back as recorded.
  structure_in_words <- function(x) {
    if (grepl("dimension\\s*\\|\\s*id", x) || grepl("slope", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      "the registered by-participant dimension slope was fitted"
    } else if (grepl("\\(\\s*1\\s*\\|\\s*id\\s*\\)", x) ||
               grepl("intercept", x, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      paste0("the by-participant dimension slope was not fitted, so this row ",
             "rests on the registered fallback of a participant intercept ",
             "only, and the comparative claim is weakened accordingly")
    } else {
      paste0("the recorded random structure matches neither the registered ",
             "slope form nor the intercept-only fallback; read it as quoted")
    }
  }
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(h2_ordinal))) {
    cat(sprintf("%s version: random structure %s; converged: %s; %s.\n",
                h2_ordinal$version[i],
                h2_ordinal$random_structure_used[i],
                as.character(h2_ordinal$converged[i]),
                structure_in_words(h2_ordinal$random_structure_used[i])))
  }
  agree <- unique(as.logical(h2_ordinal$agree_sign_and_significance))
  if (length(agree) != 1L || is.na(agree)) {
    stop("agree_sign_and_significance should be one non-NA value repeated ",
         "on every row of study1_h2_ordinal.csv; found: ",
         paste(h2_ordinal$agree_sign_and_significance, collapse = ", "))
  }
  # The agreement meets the registered condition only when both fits are
  # recorded as converged. A fit that did not converge cannot support the
  # claim.
  not_converged <- h2_ordinal$version[!(as.logical(h2_ordinal$converged) %in% TRUE)]
  cat(if (agree && length(not_converged) == 0L) {
    paste0("The two versions agree in sign and in significance, and both fits ",
           "are recorded as converged, which is the registered condition for ",
           "claiming H2.\n")
  } else if (agree) {
    paste0("The two versions agree in sign and in significance, but the ",
           paste(not_converged, collapse = " and "), " fit is not recorded as ",
           "converged, so the agreement does not meet the registered condition ",
           "for claiming H2 on this run.\n")
  } else {
    paste0("The two versions do not agree in sign and in significance; on the ",
           "registered rule H2 is reported as a failure, with the range ",
           "explanation named.\n")
  })
  h2_ordinal
}
```

## 10.10 What the design can resolve for H4

The preregistration commits to reporting what this sample can resolve,
instead of assuming the sample is large enough. For H4 the quantity most
limited by the sample is the ratio of machine-arm to human-arm
between-participant variance. It rests on two groups, of 56 and 55
participants. `Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd` section 4.1 answers by simulation.
It generates data sets of exactly this design, ten images rated by 56
human-arm and 55 machine-arm participants, from the variance components the
real fits estimated. It fits the two models of the registered H4 test to
each data set and estimates the ratio on every one. The distance between the
2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of those estimates is the sampling spread of
the ratio estimate: how far the estimate moves from one sample of this size
to the next. The spread is not the width of the bootstrap interval the
registered test reports. Nor does it say anything about that interval's
coverage, how often an interval of that kind contains the true ratio. No
interval is computed inside each simulated data set, and for a skewed
quantity such as a variance ratio the two can differ. The reading runs in one direction only.
A wide spread means a ratio near 1 could not be told apart from a ratio well
away from it. A null on H4 would then be reported as uninformative, not as
evidence that the two arms have the same between-participant spread.

```{r supp-table-h4-resolution}
# One row per dimension and setting. There are three settings. In
# null_pooled both arms share one between-participant variance. The spread on
# those rows is the sampling spread of the ratio estimate when the null is
# true, and the rejection share is the false-positive rate of the likelihood
# ratio test. In observed every component sits at its estimated value. The
# spread is the sampling spread at the ratio actually estimated, and the
# rejection share is the power against a ratio of that size. In grid the true
# ratio takes each of a set of values, with the human arm's variance held at
# its observed value. From the grid, smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct reads the
# smallest ratio the design detects with 80 per cent power (NA when the grid
# does not reach it).
#
# Column contract from the writer: dimension, setting, true_ratio_between,
# n_sim, n_used, n_failed, n_singular, n_nonfinite_ratio, n_warnings,
# mean_log_ratio, sd_log_ratio, median_ratio, ratio_q025, ratio_q975,
# ratio_spread_95, log_ratio_spread_95, lrt_reject_rate, lrt_reject_mc_se,
# interval_width_meaning, status, smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct. When the
# variance partition the simulation starts from is not on disk, the writer
# deposits a one-row ledger with status "skipped" instead. The file is
# therefore read first and rendered only if the simulation ran.
#
# The typeset table keeps the columns a reader needs to check the claim:
#   - the setting and the true ratio;
#   - the median estimate, whose gap from the true ratio is the small-sample
#     bias of the estimator;
#   - the two percentiles and their spread;
#   - the rejection share, with its Monte Carlo standard error, the
#     uncertainty in that share that comes from running a finite number of
#     simulations;
#   - the counts of singular and failed fits, singular meaning one arm's
#     variance was driven to zero, so the ratio is zero or infinite and the
#     data set is set aside;
#   - the smallest detectable grid ratio.
# A column the writer does not carry is absent from the table. If none of
# them is present, the file is rendered whole, less any long constant text
# column, which drop_long_constant_columns() from section 1 prints once above
# the table. The full CSV is deposited unchanged either way.
#
# The spread columns are ratio_spread_95 and log_ratio_spread_95. The
# writer's interval_width_meaning column states in words that the spread is
# the spread of the estimate over simulations, not a per-simulation interval.
# That column is one sentence repeated on every row and is printed once above
# the table.
remove_fragment("sup_table_h4_resolution.tex")
h4_res_pending <- "run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 4.1 (the H4 half of what the design can resolve)"
h4_res_raw     <- read_table_or_null("study1_h4_resolution.csv", h4_res_pending,
                                     stage = "robustness")

h4_res_skipped <- !is.null(h4_res_raw) && "status" %in% names(h4_res_raw) &&
  isTRUE(all(h4_res_raw$status == "skipped"))

if (is.null(h4_res_raw)) {
  record_file("output", file.path(PATH_SUP_TAB, "sup_table_h4_resolution.tex"),
              "pending", h4_res_pending)
} else if (h4_res_skipped) {
  cat("study1_h4_resolution.csv is a skipped ledger, not a result: ",
      paste(unique(as.character(h4_res_raw$note)), collapse = "; "),
      ". No table is written until the simulation has run.\n", sep = "")
  record_file("output", file.path(PATH_SUP_TAB, "sup_table_h4_resolution.tex"),
              "pending", "the simulation deposited a skipped ledger")
} else {
  h4_res_keep <- c("dimension", "setting", "true_ratio_between",
                   "median_ratio", "sd_log_ratio", "ratio_q025", "ratio_q975",
                   "ratio_spread_95", "lrt_reject_rate", "lrt_reject_mc_se",
                   "n_singular", "n_failed", "smallest_grid_ratio_at_80pct")
  render_prereg_table(
    csv_name    = "study1_h4_resolution.csv",
    tex_name    = "sup_table_h4_resolution.tex",
    caption     = "What the design can resolve for H4: the sampling spread of the estimated ratio of machine-arm to human-arm between-participant variance at this study's arm sizes, 56 and 55 participants, by simulation. Data sets of this design are generated from the estimated variance components, the two models of the registered H4 test are fitted to each, and the ratio is estimated on every one; ratio\\_q025 and ratio\\_q975 are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of those estimates across simulations and ratio\\_spread\\_95 the distance between them, the spread of the ratio estimate from one sample of this size to the next. It is not the width or the coverage of the bootstrap interval the registered test reports: no interval is computed inside each simulated data set, and for a skewed quantity such as a variance ratio the two can differ. Rows are one per dimension and setting: null\\_pooled gives both arms one common between-participant variance, so its spread is the spread of the estimate when the null is true and its rejection share (lrt\\_reject\\_rate, with the Monte Carlo standard error that comes from a finite number of simulations) is the false-positive rate of the likelihood ratio test; observed puts every component at its estimated value, so its spread is the spread at the ratio actually estimated and its rejection share is the power against a ratio of that size; grid sets the true ratio to each listed value, and smallest\\_grid\\_ratio\\_at\\_80pct is the smallest that the design detects with 80\\% power, NA where the grid does not reach it. median\\_ratio is the median estimate, whose gap from the true ratio is the estimator's small-sample bias; n\\_singular and n\\_failed count the simulated data sets set aside because one arm's variance was driven to zero or the fit errored. Where the spread is wide relative to the ratios at issue, a null on H4 is reported as uninformative rather than as evidence that the two arms' variances are equal.",
    label       = "supp_h4_resolution",
    pending_msg = h4_res_pending,
    stage       = "robustness",
    transform   = function(df) {
      df <- drop_long_constant_columns(df)
      if (any(h4_res_keep %in% names(df))) {
        df <- df %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(h4_res_keep))
      }
      df
    }
  )
}
```

## 10.11 The five registered tests on the written explanations (exploratory family)

The written explanations are asked four questions and no others, and those
questions carry five directional tests between them. The first four tests
are the denotation comparisons. They ask what the word "effort" referred to
for participants told a person made the work, and what the word "creativity"
referred to. Each comparison is one model, not a side-by-side look at two
rates. For a given arm and rating dimension, the two flags being compared
are stacked, one row per explanation and measure. The stacked flag is fitted
as a mixed logistic regression on which measure it is. A mixed logistic
regression is a model for a true-or-false outcome, here whether a fixed
search pattern fired in the explanation. Its random intercepts give each
participant and each image a baseline of its own, so one person's twenty
explanations are not counted as twenty independent observations. In the
human arm's effort explanations, visible detail is compared against time and
against skill. In the human arm's creativity explanations, the idea behind
the work (concept) is compared against visible detail (execution, measured
by the same detail pattern). Concept is also compared against familiarity
talk either way (novelty, measured by the prior-exposure pattern), which counts
both an assertion that the work looks familiar and a denial of it. The fifth
test asks what the machine-arm participants took the effort question to be
about. It asks whether prompting-and-generating talk appears more often in
that arm's effort explanations than in its creativity explanations. The
model is the same, with the flag on rating dimension, fitted within the
machine arm.

These five tests form one exploratory family. They are corrected together by
the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at .05, which controls the expected share
of false positives among the tests called positive. They stay apart from the
confirmatory family of section 10.8 and do not enter its Holm correction. No
result among them is offered in support of a prediction.

```{r supp-table-denotation-tests}
# Column contract from the writer: comparison, arm, dimension, n_responses,
# n_participants, estimate_log_odds, se, z, p_raw, p_bh, predicted_direction,
# observed_direction, note. One row per test, five rows. estimate_log_odds is
# the log-odds difference between the two measures (or, for the fifth row,
# between the two dimensions), se its standard error, and z the ratio of the
# two. p_raw is the uncorrected p-value and p_bh the Benjamini-Hochberg
# adjusted one across the five. note carries any convergence or singularity
# warning from the fit, or is blank. Both p columns match P_COL_PATTERN, so a
# very small p prints as "< 0.001" and not as 0.
denotation_caption <- paste0(
  "The five registered tests on the written explanations: an exploratory ",
  "family, corrected by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure and kept separate ",
  "from the confirmatory family and its Holm correction. Each of the first ",
  "four is one mixed logistic regression, a model for a true-or-false ",
  "outcome (here, whether a fixed search pattern fired in an explanation) ",
  "with random intercepts for participant and for image so that one ",
  "person's twenty explanations are not counted as twenty independent ",
  "observations, of the stacked flag on which measure it is, fitted within ",
  "the human-attribution arm and the named dimension: visible detail ",
  "against time and against skill in the effort explanations; the idea ",
  "behind the work (concept) against visible detail (execution) and against ",
  "familiarity talk either way (novelty) in the creativity explanations. ",
  "The fifth is the same model of prompting-and-generating talk on rating ",
  "dimension, fitted within the machine-attribution arm. The estimate is ",
  "the log-odds difference, the change in the logarithm of the odds that ",
  "the pattern fires, with its standard error (se) and z statistic; ",
  "p\\_raw is the uncorrected p-value and p\\_bh the same after the ",
  "Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the five, which controls the ",
  "expected share of false positives among the tests called positive, at ",
  ".05. The predicted direction is recorded beside the observed one, and ",
  "the note column carries any convergence or singularity warning from the ",
  "fit. No result here is offered in support of a prediction in the ",
  "confirmatory set."
)

render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_text_denotation_tests.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_denotation_tests.tex",
  caption     = denotation_caption,
  label       = "supp_denotation_tests",
  pending_msg = paste0("run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd (the five registered ",
                       "tests on the written explanations: sections 3 and 4 ",
                       "for the four denotation comparisons, section 6 for ",
                       "prompting talk across the machine arm's two dimensions)"),
  stage       = "integration"
)
```

Each of the five models gives every participant a baseline rate of their
own, but one gap between the two measures that all participants share. If
participants differ in that gap, for instance one writing almost only about
detail and another splitting detail and time evenly, the model treats those
differences as noise around a single gap, and its standard error can come
out too small. The preregistration therefore lists a sensitivity check
beside the five tests, one that changes no verdict. Each test is refitted
with the gap also free to vary by participant: a random slope for the
measure, or in the fifth test for the dimension. The refit uses the same
rows as the registered model. The table sets each registered estimate and
standard error beside the refitted ones, so a reader can see whether the
simpler structure is what carries the result.

```{r supp-table-denotation-slope-sensitivity}
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_03_Integration.Rmd section 7.2):
# comparison, role, registered_estimate_log_odds, registered_se,
# estimate_log_odds, se, z, p_raw, status, model, note. One row per test, in
# the order of the table above. registered_estimate_log_odds and
# registered_se are the estimate and standard error of the registered model;
# estimate_log_odds, se, z and p_raw come from the refit with the random
# slope. status is the writer's reading of the refit. A refit whose status
# does not permit inference keeps its estimate and carries no standard error
# or p.
#
# The typeset table keeps the comparison, the two estimates and their
# standard errors, z, p_raw and status. keep_columns_report() prints the
# role, model and note columns once on the console, beside the comparison,
# and the caption quotes the model column. p_raw matches P_COL_PATTERN, so a
# very small p prints as "< 0.001" and not as 0.
render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_text_denotation_slope_sensitivity.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_denotation_slope_sensitivity.tex",
  caption     = function(df) paste0(
    "The five registered tests on the written explanations, refitted with a ",
    "participant random slope. The registered model gives each participant a ",
    "baseline of their own but one gap that all participants share; the ",
    "refit lets the gap each test measures (between the two measures or, in ",
    "the fifth test, between the two dimensions) vary by participant. The ",
    "preregistration lists this refit as a sensitivity check that changes no ",
    "verdict, and it enters no correction family. Each refit uses the rows ",
    "its registered model saw. The columns ",
    "registered\\_estimate\\_log\\_odds and registered\\_se are the log-odds ",
    "difference and its standard error from the registered model, as in the ",
    "table above; estimate\\_log\\_odds, se and z are the same from the ",
    "refit, and p\\_raw is its uncorrected p-value. The status column is the ",
    "analysis's reading of the refit, and a refit whose status does not ",
    "permit inference carries no standard error or p. ",
    "Some growth in the standard error under the refit is the usual result, ",
    "since the refit no longer treats every participant's gap as the same ",
    "one.",
    writer_quote(df, "model", "The analysis records the models as"),
    " The full table, with the analysis's note on each fit, is deposited as ",
    "tables/study1\\_text\\_denotation\\_slope\\_sensitivity.csv."),
  label       = "supp_denotation_slope_sensitivity",
  pending_msg = paste0("run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd section 7.2 (the five ",
                       "text tests refitted with a participant random slope)"),
  transform   = function(df) keep_columns_report(
    df,
    keep = c("comparison", "registered_estimate_log_odds", "registered_se",
             "estimate_log_odds", "se", "z", "p_raw", "status"),
    key  = "comparison"),
  stage       = "integration"
)
```

## 10.12 H3: the registered equivalence test under both random-effects structures

H3 predicts that the attribution penalty does not depend on the kind of
image, figurative or non-figurative. That is a prediction of no effect, so a
non-significant interaction is not by itself evidence for it. The
preregistration pairs the ordinary significance test with an equivalence
test, which asks whether the estimate sits inside a stated bound. The
verdict comes from the two tests read together. The test is run under the
intercepts-only structure and under the maximal structure. Random slopes let
an effect vary from person to person or from image to image. A structure
that leaves out warranted random slopes gives the interaction too narrow an
interval, and a too-narrow interval makes a prediction of no effect easier
to confirm.

```{r supp-table-h3-equivalence}
# The registered rows of the H3 test: one per dimension and random-effects
# structure, with the two tests the verdict is read from and the verdict
# itself. The same file also carries rows at the wider bounds of 0.30 and
# 0.50 rating points. Those rows are descriptive sensitivity and carry no
# verdict. They are left out here, since Supplementary Table 1 already
# reports sensitivity of that kind from Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd.
#
# A fit is singular when the optimiser has driven an estimated variance or
# correlation to the edge of its range, a sign that the data cannot support
# that many parameters. The registered rule for a singular maximal fit is
# that the verdict rests on the intercepts-only structure and the output
# records which structure was used. random_structure names the structure of
# each row. fit_singular flags the singular fit. h3_claim states the
# conclusion for the dimension. Any column whose name contains
# "structure_used" is also kept by the select, so a column the writer adds to
# name the structure behind the claim is not lost. The selected rows then
# pass through drop_long_constant_columns(). A column that is one sentence
# repeated on all four rows, as the structure column is when both dimensions
# rest on the same structure, is printed once above the table. A column that
# differs by row is typeset.
#
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10):
# dimension, random_structure, bound_role, term, bound_lo, bound_hi,
# estimate, se, df, ci90_lo, ci90_hi, tost_p_lower, tost_p_upper, tost_p,
# equivalent, nhst_p, nhst_significant, fit_singular, verdict,
# alpha_per_side, h3_claim. term and alpha_per_side are constant across rows.
# bound_lo and bound_hi are fixed by the registered bound once the rows are
# filtered. tost_p is the larger of the two one-sided p-values,
# tost_p_lower and tost_p_upper, and stands for both. Those columns are
# dropped, and the caption states them. tost_p and nhst_p match
# P_COL_PATTERN, so a very small p prints as "< 0.001" and not as 0.
h3_required <- c("dimension", "random_structure", "bound_role", "estimate",
                 "se", "ci90_lo", "ci90_hi", "tost_p", "equivalent",
                 "nhst_p", "nhst_significant", "fit_singular", "verdict",
                 "h3_claim")

h3_registered_rows <- function(df) {
  missing <- setdiff(h3_required, names(df))
  if (length(missing) > 0L) {
    stop("study1_h3_equivalence.csv is missing expected columns (",
         paste(missing, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
         paste(names(df), collapse = ", "),
         ". Align Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10 (writer) with this reader.")
  }
  out <- df %>%
    filter(bound_role == "registered") %>%
    select(dimension, random_structure, matches("structure_used"),
           estimate, se, ci90_lo, ci90_hi, tost_p, equivalent,
           nhst_p, nhst_significant, fit_singular, verdict, h3_claim)
  # Two dimensions under two structures: four registered rows.
  if (nrow(out) != 4L) {
    stop("Expected four registered rows in study1_h3_equivalence.csv ",
         "(two dimensions under two structures) and found ", nrow(out),
         ". Re-run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10.")
  }
  drop_long_constant_columns(out)
}

h3_caption <- paste0(
  "H3, the registered prediction that the attribution penalty does not ",
  "depend on the kind of image (figurative or non-figurative): the ",
  "attribution-by-image-kind interaction, in rating points, tested against ",
  "the registered bound of plus or minus 0.20 rating points on each ",
  "dimension and under each of two random-effects structures. The ",
  "intercepts-only structure gives each participant and each image its own ",
  "baseline; the maximal structure also lets the image-kind difference vary ",
  "from participant to participant and the attribution penalty vary from ",
  "image to image, which widens the interval on the interaction and so ",
  "makes a prediction of no effect harder, not easier, to confirm. Each row ",
  "reads two tests together: the equivalence test, two one-sided tests of ",
  "the estimate against each end of the bound, each at .05, so the interval ",
  "shown is a 90\\% confidence interval and tost\\_p is the larger of the ",
  "two one-sided p-values (equivalent is TRUE when both ends are rejected), ",
  "and the ordinary test of whether the interaction differs from zero ",
  "(nhst\\_p, nhst\\_significant). Not significant and equivalent is ",
  "supported; significant and not equivalent is rejected; either remaining ",
  "combination is inconclusive, and the verdict column states which. H3 is ",
  "claimed only if the verdict is the same under both structures, and a ",
  "disagreement is reported as inconclusive. A singular fit is one in which ",
  "the optimiser has driven an estimated variance or correlation to the ",
  "edge of its range, a sign that the data cannot support that many ",
  "parameters; it can still carry slope variances above zero, so the ",
  "fallback below is the registered rule for such a fit and not a finding ",
  "that the slopes are absent. When the maximal fit is singular the verdict ",
  "rests on the intercepts-only structure and the table records which ",
  "structure was used: random\\_structure names the structure of each row, ",
  "fit\\_singular ",
  "flags the singular fit, and h3\\_claim states the conclusion for the ",
  "dimension. The rows at the wider bounds of 0.30 and 0.50 rating points ",
  "in the same file are descriptive sensitivity, carry no verdict, and are ",
  "left out here. A passed equivalence test stands on its own, because the ",
  "two one-sided tests hold the rate of wrongly declaring equivalence at .05 ",
  "on each side whatever their power; a failed one is read against the ",
  "simulated power of the equivalence test at the registered bound under a ",
  "true interaction of zero, deposited in ",
  "tables/study1\\_h3\\_equivalence\\_power.csv and rendered in the table ",
  "that follows."
)

h3_table <- render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_h3_equivalence.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_h3_equivalence.tex",
  caption     = h3_caption,
  label       = "supp_h3_equivalence",
  pending_msg = paste0("run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.10 (H3 equivalence ",
                       "test under both random-effects structures)"),
  transform   = h3_registered_rows,
  stage       = "quant"
)

# The conclusion is stated per dimension, as the writer's h3_claim gives it,
# so a pass on one dimension is not read as H3 holding on both. When the
# claim is one sentence on all four rows, drop_long_constant_columns() has
# already printed it once above the table.
if (!is.null(h3_table) && "h3_claim" %in% names(h3_table)) {
  h3_table %>%
    distinct(dimension, h3_claim) %>%
    mutate(line = paste0("H3, ", dimension, ": ", h3_claim)) %>%
    pull(line) %>%
    paste(collapse = "\n") %>%
    cat("\n")
}
```

The verdict in that table is read with the power of the equivalence test
beside it. A pass stands on its own. The two one-sided tests hold the rate
of wrongly declaring equivalence at .05 on each side whatever their power,
so low power makes a pass unlikely but not wrong. A fail is informative only
when the design would usually have passed under a true interaction of zero.
`Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd` section 4 checks this by simulation. It generates
data sets of this design from the primary model with the interaction fixed
at zero and refits the model to each. The share of data sets on which the
two one-sided tests pass at the registered bound is the power of the
equivalence test. When that share falls below 80 per cent, a failed
equivalence test is reported as uninformative. That is a statement about the
width of the interval this design produces, not about the interaction. The
same simulation is repeated with the interaction fixed at a small nonzero
value, as sensitivity. Every simulated interval is also read against the
wider bounds of 0.30 and 0.50 rating points, so the table also shows how far
the bound would have to widen before the design usually passed.

```{r supp-table-h3-equivalence-power}
# One row per dimension, true interaction and bound: the registered bound of
# 0.20 rating points and the two descriptive bounds of 0.30 and 0.50, each
# under a true interaction of zero and of a small nonzero value. Two
# dimensions, two true interactions and three bounds make twelve rows.
#
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 4, chunk
# h3-equivalence-power): dimension, true_interaction, bound,
# bound_is_registered, equivalence_power, mc_se, ci_lo, ci_hi,
# analytic_power, n_sim, n_used, n_failed, n_singular, n_warnings, n_inside,
# se_deposited, df_deposited, halfwidth_90, mean_estimate, sd_estimate,
# mean_se, alpha_per_side, registered_test_passed, h3_claim,
# h3_structure_used, verdict_source, power_registered_bound_true_zero,
# h3_equivalence_informative, informative_rule, power_target, seed,
# runtime_minutes_all_cells, analysis_type. The writer deposits no skipped
# ledger. The file is either absent, and this chunk prints a pending line,
# or complete. A missing column or an NA power therefore stops the chunk.
#
# The typeset table keeps the columns a reader needs to check the claim:
#   - the cell: dimension, true interaction, bound, and whether the bound is
#     the registered one;
#   - the simulated power, with its Monte Carlo standard error (the amount
#     the share would move from one run of the simulation to the next purely
#     because the data sets are random draws) and its exact binomial
#     interval;
#   - the analytic approximation from the deposited standard error, as a
#     check on both;
#   - the counts of refits used, singular and failed;
#   - the three columns that carry the reading: whether the registered test
#     passed, the power at the registered bound under a true zero (one value
#     per dimension, repeated on its rows), and the informative flag, TRUE on
#     a pass and on a fail only when that power reaches the target.
# The rule the flag applies is a long constant text column, which
# drop_long_constant_columns() from section 1 prints once above the table.
# The full CSV is deposited unchanged.
h3_pow_required <- c("dimension", "true_interaction", "bound",
                     "bound_is_registered", "equivalence_power", "mc_se",
                     "ci_lo", "ci_hi", "analytic_power", "n_used",
                     "n_singular", "n_failed", "registered_test_passed",
                     "power_registered_bound_true_zero",
                     "h3_equivalence_informative")

h3_pow_rows <- function(df) {
  missing <- setdiff(h3_pow_required, names(df))
  if (length(missing) > 0L) {
    stop("study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv is missing expected columns (",
         paste(missing, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
         paste(names(df), collapse = ", "),
         ". Align Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 4 (writer) with this reader.")
  }
  # Two dimensions, two true interactions, three bounds: twelve rows.
  if (nrow(df) != 12L) {
    stop("Expected twelve rows in study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv ",
         "(two dimensions, two true interactions, three bounds) and found ",
         nrow(df), ". Re-run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 4.")
  }
  if (anyNA(df$equivalence_power)) {
    stop("study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv carries an NA equivalence_power. ",
         "Re-run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 4 rather than print around it.")
  }
  df <- drop_long_constant_columns(df)
  df %>%
    arrange(dimension, true_interaction, bound) %>%
    select(all_of(h3_pow_required))
}

h3_pow_caption <- paste0(
  "Power of the registered H3 equivalence test, by simulation, as design ",
  "sensitivity and not observed power: data sets of this design, ten images ",
  "rated by 56 human-arm and 55 machine-arm participants, are drawn from the ",
  "primary model with its estimated variance components and the ",
  "attribution-by-image-kind interaction fixed at the stated true value ",
  "(true\\_interaction, in rating points: zero, and a small nonzero value as ",
  "sensitivity), the model is refitted to each, and equivalence\\_power is ",
  "the share of data sets on which the 90\\% interval on the interaction lies ",
  "inside the stated bound (bound, in rating points; bound\\_is\\_registered ",
  "marks the registered bound of 0.20, the others being the descriptive ",
  "bounds of 0.30 and 0.50). mc\\_se is the Monte Carlo standard error of ",
  "that share, the amount it would move from one run of the simulation to ",
  "the next purely because the data sets are random draws, and ci\\_lo and ",
  "ci\\_hi its exact binomial interval; analytic\\_power is the same ",
  "probability worked out without simulation from the standard error the ",
  "registered test deposited, as a check on both. n\\_used, n\\_singular and ",
  "n\\_failed count the refits kept, the refits in which a variance was ",
  "driven to zero (kept, since the interval is still valid), and the refits ",
  "that errored (set aside). registered\\_test\\_passed is the verdict of the ",
  "registered test on the structure that carries it, ",
  "power\\_registered\\_bound\\_true\\_zero is the power at the registered ",
  "bound under a true interaction of zero, one value per dimension, and ",
  "h3\\_equivalence\\_informative is the flag that governs how the verdict is ",
  "reported: TRUE on a pass, because the two one-sided tests hold the rate ",
  "of wrongly declaring equivalence at .05 on each side whatever their power, ",
  "and on a fail only when that power reaches 80\\%, below which the design ",
  "would usually have failed even if the two penalties were identical and ",
  "the fail is reported as uninformative."
)

render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_h3_equivalence_power.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_h3_equivalence_power.tex",
  caption     = h3_pow_caption,
  label       = "supp_h3_equivalence_power",
  pending_msg = paste0("run Study1_04_Robustness.Rmd section 4 (chunk ",
                       "h3-equivalence-power, the power of the H3 ",
                       "equivalence test)"),
  transform   = h3_pow_rows,
  stage       = "robustness"
)
```

## 10.13 Two checks run in every study

Two further quantities on the written explanations are registered as
checks. Each runs unchanged in every study where the rating exists and is
reported wherever it falls. Neither is among the four predictions of the
preregistration, and neither enters its confirmatory family. Both take their
text side from `Study1_02_Text.ipynb`, whose measurement step runs before
the condition or the rating is joined to the text. The arm and the rating
are joined only in `Study1_03_Integration.Rmd`, which deposits the two
tables rendered here. No step in either check requires a person to read or
judge an individual explanation.

The first check asks how much of the rating, and of the arm, can be
recovered from the words. It is descriptive and carries no verdict. It
states how closely the explanations track the rating a participant had just
given. Each explanation was written after its rating, so no text measure in
this project is read as a mechanism behind the rating. The notebook reduces
every explanation to counts of its content words, the words left once a
fixed list of function words such as "the" and "of" is removed. It exports
those counts with nothing else attached. The integration file then predicts
the rating from the counts, and the arm from the counts. Each model is
scored only on explanations it was not fitted to, and each participant stays
whole on one side of that split. Each result is compared against what the
same procedure recovers when the thing to be predicted has been shuffled.
Beside the arm result, the file reports how well the rating alone recovers
the arm. It then asks whether the words add to the rating. A model of the
arm on the rating and the words together is scored on the same held-out
participants as the rating-only model, and the paired difference between
the two scores is reported with its interval. Two stand-alone scores,
however close, say nothing by themselves about whether the words carry
information beyond the rating. The paired difference is the quantity that
does.

The second check is the text version of H4, the prediction that under the
machine label a rating is more a property of the person judging and less a
property of the particular picture. If that is so, participants under the
machine label should reuse their own words across the ten images more than
participants under the human label. The notebook writes, for every
explanation, the set of its content words. For each participant and
dimension, the integration file measures two overlaps. One is how much that
participant's ten explanations share words with one another. The other is
how much they share with what other participants wrote about the same
picture. The file compares the excess of the first over the second between
arms, holding the length of the explanations constant, since overlap falls
as texts get longer. The two dimensions are corrected together by the Holm
procedure (the tests are ordered from the smallest p-value upward and each
is compared against a threshold that starts strictest and relaxes as earlier
tests pass). Each is read as supported, opposite direction or inconclusive.

For Study 1 the first check is reported as a quantity already partly known,
not as a prediction. The recoverability of the rating from the text was
computed in earlier exploratory work on this study, with a different method.
That work also tried a version of the second check built on sentence
embeddings (numerical representations of a sentence's meaning produced by a
language model), and that version did not survive resampling. The
word-overlap version rendered here had not been run when the preregistration
was written.

```{r supp-table-text-recoverability}
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_03_Integration.Rmd, the
# recoverability check): one row per dimension, target and predictor set.
# The rows are rating from words, arm from words, arm from rating, arm from
# rating plus words, and the incremental row. The incremental row is the
# paired difference in AUC between the rating-plus-words model and the
# rating-only model on the same held-out participants. AUC is the
# probability that a randomly chosen machine-arm explanation is scored as
# more machine-like than a randomly chosen human-arm one: 0.5 for chance, 1
# for perfect separation. The columns are
# statistic, estimate, ci_low, ci_high, null_95th, n_perm, n_folds,
# n_features, seed, then bookkeeping counts and two description columns,
# model and permutation. estimate is r on the rating rows, the AUC on the arm
# rows and the AUC difference on the incremental row. ci_low and ci_high give
# its 95 percent interval from resampling participants. null_95th is the 95th
# percentile of the permutation null, the distribution of the statistic when
# the outcome is shuffled, and n_perm is the number of permutations behind
# it. The registered count is 200, with 100 allowed when the run exceeds its
# time budget, and the writer records which was run. A row without a
# permutation null carries NA in those columns.
#
# The text side of this check is two files. nlp/study1_text_wordcounts.csv
# has one row per explanation and word, with the count of that word, for
# words in at least two explanations. nlp/study1_text_vocabulary.csv lists
# the words and the number of explanations each appears in. Neither carries
# a condition, a rating or the text itself. The join to the arm and the
# rating happens in the integration file alone. The registered floor of five
# explanations is applied there, inside each training fold, so the held-out
# participants have no say in which words enter the model.
#
# The caption quotes the writer's permutation column, so each null is
# described in the writer's own words. The typeset table keeps the
# row-identifying and statistic columns. The description columns and the
# bookkeeping counts differ between rows, so drop_long_constant_columns()
# would remove nothing. keep_columns_report() prints them once on the
# console, beside the row keys, instead. No kept column name matches
# P_COL_PATTERN, so no cell here is formatted as a p-value.
recoverability_caption <- function(df) {
  shuffles <- if (all(c("target", "permutation") %in% names(df))) {
    s <- df %>%
      filter(!is.na(permutation)) %>%
      distinct(target, permutation)
    if (nrow(s) > 0L) {
      paste0("The shuffle behind each null, as the integration file describes it: ",
             paste(sprintf("for the %s, %s", latex_escape(s$target),
                           latex_escape(s$permutation)), collapse = "; "),
             ". ")
    } else ""
  } else ""
  paste0(
    "How far the rating and the arm can be recovered from the words: a ",
    "registered check, run in every study where the rating exists, ",
    "descriptive and in no correction family. Each explanation is reduced to ",
    "counts of its content words, lower-cased runs of letters and ",
    "apostrophes with a fixed list of function words such as the, and and of ",
    "removed; inside each training fold the words that appear in at least ",
    "five of the training explanations are kept, so the held-out ",
    "participants have no say in which words enter the model. The notebook ",
    "that counts them is computed before the condition or the rating is ",
    "joined to the text. Rating from words is a ridge regression of the ",
    "rating on those counts, a linear model that shrinks its many word ",
    "coefficients toward zero by an amount chosen by inner cross-validation ",
    "so that it does not simply memorise the explanations it was fitted to, ",
    "fitted per dimension with ten outer folds grouped by participant, so that ",
    "no participant's explanations sit in both the fitting and the scoring ",
    "part of any fold. Its statistic r is the correlation between predicted ",
    "and observed rating over the held-out explanations only, where 0 is no ",
    "relation and 1 a perfect one (an out-of-fold r can fall below 0 when the ",
    "held-out predictions run against the observed ratings), with a 95\\% ",
    "interval from 2,000 resamples of participants. Arm from words is the ",
    "same with a ridge logistic regression of the arm on the counts, and its ",
    "statistic is the AUC, the area under the receiver operating ",
    "characteristic (ROC) curve: the probability that a randomly chosen ",
    "machine-arm explanation is scored as more machine-like than a randomly ",
    "chosen human-arm one, 0.5 for chance and 1 for perfect separation. Arm ",
    "from rating is a logistic regression of the arm on the rating alone with ",
    "the same folds. Arm from rating plus words adds the word counts to the ",
    "rating, and the incremental row is its AUC minus the AUC of arm from ",
    "rating, the two scored on the same held-out participants, with an ",
    "interval from resampling participants: it is the quantity that says ",
    "whether the words carry information about the arm beyond the rating. ",
    "The stand-alone AUCs are descriptive references, and the difference ",
    "between them is not that quantity. null\\_95th is the permutation null: ",
    "the outcome is shuffled so that the words have nothing real to predict, ",
    "the whole procedure is rerun, and the 95th percentile of the statistics ",
    "over n\\_perm shuffles is the value the observed statistic must exceed ",
    "to be read as signal rather than chance. Each shuffle is restricted so ",
    "that it keeps the structure of the data rather than scattering single ",
    "responses: the arm label moves between whole participants, and the ",
    "rating null keeps each participant's ratings together across the ten ",
    "images. ",
    shuffles,
    "n\\_folds is the number of outer folds, n\\_features the number of word ",
    "columns the integration file records, and seed the random seed of the run."
  )
}

render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_text_recoverability.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_text_recoverability.tex",
  caption     = recoverability_caption,
  label       = "supp_text_recoverability",
  pending_msg = paste0("run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd (the recoverability ",
                       "check: rating and arm from the word counts in ",
                       "nlp/study1_text_wordcounts.csv, which ",
                       "Study1_02_Text.ipynb writes)"),
  transform   = function(df) keep_columns_report(
    df,
    keep = c("dimension", "target", "predictors", "estimate", "ci_low",
             "ci_high", "null_95th", "n_perm", "n_folds", "n_features",
             "seed"),
    key  = c("dimension", "target", "predictors")
  ),
  stage       = "integration"
)
```

```{r supp-table-text-selfsimilarity}
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_03_Integration.Rmd, within-person
# word overlap by arm): one row per dimension and quantity. The registered
# comparison row carries the arm difference in self_minus_stranger from the
# length-adjusted model, its interval from resampling participants, p_holm
# (its p-value after the Holm correction across the two dimensions), and the
# reading (supported, opposite direction or inconclusive). The description
# rows carry the raw overlaps by arm. The writer names its own columns, and
# this chunk does not check them: a column reaches the typeset table under
# its deposited name. The typeset table keeps the row-identifying and
# statistic columns, an unadjusted p-value column when there is one, p_holm
# and the reading. keep_columns_report() prints the model string, the
# predicted direction and the participant counts once on the console. p_holm
# matches P_COL_PATTERN, so a very small p prints as "< 0.001" and not as 0.
#
# The text side of this check is nlp/study1_text_tokens.csv, one row per
# explanation with its distinct content words and no condition or rating
# column. The integration file computes the self and stranger overlaps from
# those words, so the stranger baseline is rebuilt from the resampled
# participants in every bootstrap replicate. The arm is joined there alone.
selfsimilarity_caption <- paste0(
  "Within-person word overlap by arm, the text version of H4: a registered ",
  "check, run in every study where the rating exists, with a predicted ",
  "direction; its two dimensions are corrected together by the Holm ",
  "procedure, in which the tests are ordered from the smallest p-value upward ",
  "and each is compared against a threshold that starts strictest and relaxes ",
  "as earlier tests pass, and are kept apart from the confirmatory family. ",
  "For each ",
  "participant and dimension, self\\_overlap is the mean Jaccard overlap ",
  "across that participant's ten explanations, over all 45 pairs of them, ",
  "where the Jaccard overlap of two explanations is the number of content ",
  "words they share divided by the number of content words in either, so 0 ",
  "means no word in common and 1 the same set of words. The stranger ",
  "baseline, stranger\\_overlap, is the same overlap between each of that ",
  "participant's explanations and the explanations other participants wrote ",
  "for the same image and dimension, averaged over the ten images: how much ",
  "two people writing about the same picture share by default. ",
  "self\\_minus\\_stranger, the excess of a participant's own reuse over that ",
  "baseline, is the quantity compared; the notebook that writes each ",
  "explanation's content words never sees the condition or the rating. The ",
  "arm difference is from a linear model of self\\_minus\\_stranger on arm ",
  "with the mean number of content words per explanation as a covariate, a ",
  "variable held constant in the model because the overlap statistic falls ",
  "as texts get longer, with a 95\\% interval from 2,000 resamples of ",
  "participants in which the stranger baseline is rebuilt from the ",
  "resampled participants each time, so the interval carries the ",
  "uncertainty of the reference group as well as that of the participants ",
  "compared. The prediction is that participants told a machine made the ",
  "work reuse their own words more. p\\_holm is the p-value of the arm ",
  "difference after the Holm correction across the two dimensions, and ",
  "reading states the result: supported when the corrected test rejects in ",
  "the predicted direction, opposite direction when it rejects in the other ",
  "direction, and inconclusive otherwise. An inconclusive reading, which ",
  "includes any interval that contains zero, is not evidence that the arms ",
  "reuse their words equally. The raw self\\_overlap by arm is reported ",
  "beside it as description."
)

render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.tex",
  caption     = selfsimilarity_caption,
  label       = "supp_text_selfsimilarity",
  pending_msg = paste0("run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd (within-person word ",
                       "overlap by arm, from nlp/study1_text_tokens.csv, ",
                       "which Study1_02_Text.ipynb writes)"),
  transform   = function(df) keep_columns_report(
    df,
    keep = c("dimension", "role", "quantity", "estimate", "ci_lo", "ci_hi",
             intersect(c("p_raw", "p", "p_value", "p.value"), names(df)),
             "p_holm", "n_valid", "reading"),
    key  = c("dimension", "role", "quantity")
  ),
  stage       = "integration"
)
```

---

# 11. Further analyses of the ratings and the explanations

The tables in this section sit beside the registered set. None of them is
among the four registered predictions or the five registered tests on the
written explanations. The first checks one item of the rating instrument.
The rest describe the written explanations. They use word norms published
by other laboratories (average ratings that large panels gave individual
words on scales such as unhappy to happy), a topic model fitted to the word
counts, and the weights of the recoverability models of section 10.13. Each
is computed from the blind measurement files of `Study1_02_Text.ipynb`,
which never see the condition or the rating. Each is joined to the arm and
the rating only in `Study1_03_Integration.Rmd`. No step requires a person to
read or judge an individual explanation. No language model reads or codes an
explanation for any measure. One check on the topic model, described in
section 11.4, uses a pretrained sentence-embedding model, and nothing
reported rests on it.

## 11.1 The effort item with different scale wording

The ten effort items share one five-point scale except the first figurative
item, whose top two labels differ: there 4 reads "A lot of effort involved"
and 5 "Significant effort involved", where the other nine read 4
"Significant effort involved" and 5 "A great deal of effort involved" (the
survey definition file, `qualtrics/Final_-_AI_Copyright_-_Study_1.qsf`,
question 1FigureEff). The ratings are scored as recorded, 1 to 5, on every
item. The table asks whether the registered contrasts depend on that one item
by recomputing them with it set aside. It is a sensitivity analysis and
changes neither the scoring nor the sample of the registered tests.

```{r supp-table-item-sensitivity}
# Column contract from the writer (Study1_01_Quant.Rmd, the instrument
# sensitivity for 1FigureEff): hypothesis, quantity, sample, n_ratings,
# estimate, se, df, ci_low, ci_high, p, difference_from_full,
# random_structure, converged, singular, fit_error, lme4_messages, note. One
# row per contrast and sample: the full sample, the sample with the item set
# aside, and for H2 also the sample with the whole image set aside.
#
# Typeset whole, the table is too wide for the page. The typeset table keeps
# the analysis (hypothesis and sample), the estimate, its standard error and
# its interval. The caption names each hypothesis's contrast in the writer's
# words, from the quantity column. keep_columns_report() prints every other
# column once on the console, beside the hypothesis and the sample, and the
# caption points to the deposited CSV for them. The sample column holds a
# phrase on every row and is set at a fixed width, so it wraps.
item_sensitivity_caption <- function(df) {
  contrasts <- if (all(c("hypothesis", "quantity") %in% names(df))) {
    q <- df %>% distinct(hypothesis, quantity)
    paste0(" The contrast of each hypothesis, as the writer names it: ",
           paste(sprintf("%s, %s", latex_escape(q$hypothesis),
                         latex_escape(q$quantity)), collapse = "; "),
           ".")
  } else ""
  paste0(
    "The registered contrasts with the first figurative effort item set ",
    "aside. That item's top two scale labels differ from those of the other ",
    "nine effort items (4 = A lot of effort involved and 5 = Significant ",
    "effort involved, where the others read 4 = Significant effort involved ",
    "and 5 = A great deal of effort involved); its ratings are scored 1 to 5 ",
    "as recorded. Each row names the hypothesis and the sample the contrast ",
    "is computed on, as the writer records them, with the estimate in rating ",
    "points, its standard error (se) and its 95\\% confidence interval ",
    "(ci\\_low, ci\\_high).",
    contrasts,
    " A sensitivity analysis, not a registered test: the registered scoring ",
    "and sample are unchanged. The full table, with the number of ratings, ",
    "the degrees of freedom, the p-value, the difference from the full ",
    "sample, the random-effects structure and the fit status of each row, is ",
    "deposited as tables/study1\\_item\\_sensitivity.csv.")
}

render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_item_sensitivity.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_item_sensitivity.tex",
  caption     = item_sensitivity_caption,
  label       = "supp_item_sensitivity",
  pending_msg = paste0("run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd (the item sensitivity for the ",
                       "first figurative effort item)"),
  transform   = function(df) keep_columns_report(
    df,
    keep = c("hypothesis", "sample", "estimate", "se", "ci_low", "ci_high"),
    key  = c("hypothesis", "sample")),
  stage       = "quant",
  col_widths  = c(sample = "5cm")
)
```

## 11.2 Familiarity talk and the creativity rating, within and between participants

Section 4.3 of the integration file relates familiarity talk in the creativity
explanations to the creativity rating. A participant who often says a work
looks familiar may also rate everything lower, so one coefficient on the
familiarity categories mixes two things: whether a participant rates an image
lower when they call that image familiar (the within-person part), and
whether participants who use familiarity talk more often rate lower overall
(the between-person part). This table reports the two parts separately,
within each arm. Neither part is a cause of the rating, because each
explanation was written after its rating.

```{r supp-table-text-novelty-within-between}
# Rendered as the writer in Study1_03_Integration.Rmd deposits it, less any
# long constant text column. When the writer has a model column, the caption
# quotes it, so the decomposition is described in the writer's terms.
render_prereg_table(
  csv_name    = "study1_text_novelty_within_between.csv",
  tex_name    = "sup_table_text_novelty_within_between.tex",
  caption     = function(df) paste0(
    "Familiarity talk and the creativity rating, within and between ",
    "participants, by arm. Each familiarity category of the prior-exposure ",
    "measure enters the model as two terms: the participant's share of ",
    "explanations in that category (the between-person part) and each ",
    "explanation's departure from that share (the within-person part). The ",
    "within-person coefficient asks whether a participant rates an image ",
    "lower when calling that image familiar than when not; the between-person ",
    "coefficient asks whether participants who use the category more often ",
    "rate lower overall. Each explanation was written after its rating, so ",
    "neither coefficient is a cause of the rating.",
    writer_quote(df, "model", "The analysis records the model as")),
```
